definition_zh: 锤子；锤打；猛烈抨击
definition_en: a tool with a heavy head for driving nails, to hit something with it, or to attack something strongly
core_image: 铁锤重重落在钉头上
scene: 他用锤子把钉子敲进去。 He drove the nail in with a hammer.
sceneCN: 这里 hammer 是「锤子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用锤子把钉子敲进去。

derivatives.zh: 锤打；惨败
锤头；双髻鲨

senses.title: Nail-driving tool
senses.definition: a tool with a heavy head used for driving nails
senses.definitionCN: 装有重头、用来敲钉子的工具
senses.example: He drove the nail in with a hammer.
senses.exampleCN: 他用锤子把钉子敲进去。
senses.why: The tool is the basic concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 工具本身，是最基本的具体义项。

senses.title: Strike with a hammer
senses.definition: to hit something with a hammer or as if with one
senses.definitionCN: 用锤子或像用锤子那样敲击
senses.example: She hammered the metal flat.
senses.exampleCN: 她把金属锤平。
senses.why: The tool name became the verb of using it.
senses.whyCN: 工具名称转为使用工具的动作。

senses.title: Attack in words
senses.definition: to attack or criticise someone strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈攻击或批评某人
senses.example: The critics hammered the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者猛烈抨击新计划。
senses.why: Repeated blows became repeated criticism.
senses.whyCN: 反复的敲击，变成了反复的批评。

intro.en: Hammer comes from Old English hamor, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: hammer 来自古英语 hamor，源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root named a stone or striking tool.
items.cn: 该词根指石头或敲击工具。

items.en: Hamor meant a hammer.
items.cn: hamor 意为锤子。

items.en: Hammer kept the tool sense and gained the verb.
items.cn: hammer 保留工具义，并发展出动词用法。

items.en: The verb extended to repeated effort.
items.cn: 动词义扩展到反复努力。

items.en: It came to mean strong criticism.
items.cn: 它转而表示强烈的批评。

note.en: Hammer is compared with look-alike words and other striking tools.
note.cn: 把 hammer 与形近词以及其他敲击工具作比较。

definition_zh: 重担；负担；使负担
definition_en: a heavy load that is hard to carry
core_image: 山路上背着柴捆弯着腰的人
scene: 山路很陡，柴捆压得他弯着腰。 The load was a heavy burden on his back.
sceneCN: 这里 burden 是「重担」（第 1 个义项：沉重难负的实物负荷）；句意是那捆柴是他背上的重担。

derivatives.zh: 繁重的，令人负担沉重的
卸下负担；倾诉心事

senses.title: A heavy physical load
senses.definition: a load that is heavy to carry
senses.definitionCN: 重得难以搬运的负荷
senses.example: The load was a heavy burden on his back.
senses.exampleCN: 那捆柴是他背上的重担。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from a word for carrying.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自表示「承载」的词。

senses.title: A difficult duty or worry
senses.definition: something difficult that you must bear or deal with
senses.definitionCN: 必须承受或处理的艰难事物
senses.example: Caring for four children is a real burden.
senses.exampleCN: 照顾四个孩子是真正的负担。
senses.why: Duty and worry weigh on the mind as loads weigh on the back.
senses.whyCN: 责任与忧虑压在心上，正如重物压在背上。

senses.title: To place a load on someone
senses.definition: to give someone a heavy duty or worry
senses.definitionCN: 把沉重的责任或忧虑加给某人
senses.example: Do not burden her with this news tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚别用这个消息给她添负担。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for putting the load on another.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指把重物压到别人身上。

definition_zh: 修剪；整理；削减；整齐的；修长的
definition_en: to cut a small amount from something to make it neat, or to reduce an amount; neat and well shaped
core_image: 一把剪刀沿着边线走一圈，多出来的毛边落在地上
scene: 花园里，园丁拿长剪沿着绿篱一路剪过去，剪口平得像一条线。 He trims the hedge every Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里 trim 是「修剪」（第 1 个义项：剪去多余部分使其整齐）；句意为他每周六早上修剪绿篱。剪刀沿线走、毛边落地的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「修剪；装饰边；配料」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「修剪者；修剪工具」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「整齐；整洁」

senses.title: To cut something neat
senses.definition: to cut a small amount off something so that it looks tidy
senses.definitionCN: 剪掉一点使某物看起来整齐
senses.example: She trimmed the rose bushes back.
senses.exampleCN: 她把玫瑰丛修剪了一遍。
senses.why: The old verb means to make ready or to arrange, and neat cutting is the way such arranging is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个古动词意为「整理、备好」，而剪整齐正是整理的做法。

senses.title: To reduce an amount
senses.definition: to make a sum, a list, or a text smaller by removing parts
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一部分，使金额、清单或文字变小
senses.example: The council trimmed the spending plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会削减了开支计划。
senses.why: Cutting a hedge and cutting a budget are the same motion: taking off what sticks out.
senses.whyCN: 剪树篱与削预算都是同一个动作：把多出来的部分去掉。

senses.title: To decorate an edge
senses.definition: to add a border or ornament to the edge of something
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的边上加饰边或装饰
senses.example: The dress is trimmed with lace.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子镶了花边。
senses.why: The word also meant to fit out or equip, and decorating an edge is part of that outfitting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也曾表示装配、置办，而给边镶饰正是装配的一部分。

senses.title: Neat and well shaped
senses.definition: looking neat, slim, and in good order
senses.definitionCN: 看起来整洁、匀称、有精神
senses.example: He keeps a trim little garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他把小花园打理得很整齐。
senses.why: What has been trimmed looks trim: the adjective is the result of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 被修剪过的东西显得整齐：形容词就是动词的结果。

senses.title: To adjust the balance of a boat
senses.definition: to arrange the load or sails of a boat so that it sits level
senses.definitionCN: 调整船的负载或帆，使船身平稳
senses.example: The crew trimmed the sails before the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起前船员调好了帆。
senses.why: Balancing a boat is tidying a different edge, so the same word serves on water.
senses.whyCN: 给船找平是在整理另一条边，于是同一个词也用在水上。

intro.en: The verb is an old English word for making ready or arranging, and neat cutting is its oldest surviving sense.
intro.cn: 这个动词是古英语里表示准备、整理的老词，剪整齐是它保存下来的最早义项。

items.en: Trymman means to make firm, to strengthen, or to arrange a thing.
items.cn: 古英语 trymman 意为使牢固、增强，或把事物安排好。

items.en: The word narrows towards tidying edges, and is used of hair, cloth, and hedges.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐收窄到整理边缘，用于头发、布料与树篱。

items.en: Commerce gives it the sense of cutting down a sum or a staff.
items.cn: 商业给了它削减金额或人员的义项。

items.en: Nautical use keeps an older sense of setting a load or sail in balance.
items.cn: 航海用法保留了「把负载或帆调平衡」的较老义项。

items.en: The adjective grows from the noun, naming what has just been made neat.
items.cn: 形容词由名词生出，用来指刚被弄整齐的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in spelling or root, while the near-meaning group names other cuts and states of neatness.
note.cn: 形近组汇集拼写或词根相近的短词，近义组列出其他剪切与整洁状态。

definition_zh: 直立的；竖立的；正直的；诚实的；立式（钢琴）
definition_en: standing straight up, or honest and of good character
core_image: 一根木杆笔直地立在雪地里
scene: 雪后的院子里，晾衣杆笔直插着，风吹也没倾斜。 The old post stood upright in the snow.
sceneCN: 这里 upright 是「立着的」（第 1 个义项：竖直、不歪）；句意为那根旧木杆直直地立在雪里。木杆笔直立着的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「正直地；笔直地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「正直；直立」
复合词的前一部分，义为「向上」
复合词的后一部分，义为「直的；正当的」

senses.title: Standing straight up
senses.definition: positioned vertically, with the top directly above the base
senses.definitionCN: 顶端正对底端的竖直摆放
senses.example: He put the box upright against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子竖着靠在墙边。
senses.why: The compound joins up and right in its old sense of straight, so upright means standing straight up.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词由 up 与 right（古义「直的」）合起来，意思就是「笔直地立着」。

senses.title: Sitting or standing with a straight back
senses.definition: used of a person whose back is straight and not bent
senses.definitionCN: 形容人背脊挺直不弯
senses.example: She sat upright throughout the whole interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中她都坐得笔直。
senses.why: A spine held straight is the body applying the vertical line of a standing post.
senses.whyCN: 把脊背挺直，就是身体在实践一根立杆的垂直线。

senses.title: Honest in character
senses.definition: used of people who follow what is right and fair
senses.definitionCN: 形容按是非公道行事的人
senses.example: He was an upright man who never took a bribe.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个从不受贿的正直人。
senses.why: The picture of a body that does not bend yields the moral sense: a character that does not lean either.
senses.whyCN: 身体不弯的画面生出道德义：品行也不肯向哪一边歪。

senses.title: Not lying on its side
senses.definition: used of objects stored or carried vertically
senses.definitionCN: 形容竖着存放或搬运的物件
senses.example: Keep the bottles upright in the box.
senses.exampleCN: 把瓶子竖着放进箱子里。
senses.why: An object placed on its base instead of its side repeats the core picture exactly.

examples.en: Please keep the crate upright while you carry it.

examples.en: The children sat upright as the teacher came in.

sensesIntro.en: One straight line from base to top gives the posture, then the honest character, then the standing object.

core_image: 两枚形状相同的印章，在同一张纸上压出同样的印痕
scene: 设计评审会上，第一组把图标改成圆角。 The second team did likewise, keeping the same corner radius and the same grid spacing as the first.
sceneCN: 这里 likewise 是「以同样的方式」（第 1 个义项：方式相同）；句意：第二组也照样做，沿用和第一组一样的圆角与网格间距。图中可辨识物件：两组并排的界面草图、同一套圆角网格、配色卡；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Same manner: in the same way
senses.titleCN: 同样方式：照着同一套做法
senses.definition: in the same way or by the same method as someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 以与别人或别的事物相同的方式或方法
senses.example: She folded the map carefully, and he did likewise.
senses.exampleCN: 她仔细折好地图，他也照样做了。
senses.why: The word joins like, 'having the same form', to wise, 'manner'. The first sense is therefore the plain arithmetic of the compound: same form plus manner equals same way of doing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示“具有相同形体”的 like 与表示“方式”的 wise 合在一起。因此第一个义项就是这层构词关系的直接结果：相同形体加方式，等于相同的做法。

senses.title: Addition: the same is true of the second item
senses.definition: also or too, used when a second person or thing shares the same action, quality, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 也、同样，用于第二个人或物享有同一动作、性质或处境时
senses.example: The first proposal was too costly; the second was likewise rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 第一份提案成本太高；第二份也同样被否决了。
senses.why: Repeating an action in the same way easily becomes repeating the same verdict. The adverb slides from describing how something is done to asserting that the same predicate applies again.
senses.whyCN: 用同样的方式重复一个动作，很容易变成重复同一个结论。这个词于是从描述“怎么做”，滑向断定“同样的说法对第二项也成立”。

senses.title: Parallel clause marker: a matching statement follows
senses.titleCN: 平行句标记：引出结构对应的下一句
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, used to introduce a statement that runs parallel to the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，引出与上一句结构或逻辑平行的陈述
senses.example: The north wing needs repair. Likewise, the roof must be replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 北翼需要修缮。同样地，屋顶也必须更换。
senses.why: Once the adverb sits at the head of a clause, it stops modifying a single verb and starts organizing discourse: the next clause is offered as a second panel of the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词移到从句开头，它就不再修饰单个动词，而开始组织语篇：下一句被当作同一幅图的第二块面板呈现出来。

senses.title: Reciprocal reply: the same to you
senses.definition: in conversation, a short reply meaning 'the same to you' or 'I feel the same'
senses.definitionCN: 口语中简短回应，意为“你也一样”或“我也有同感”
senses.example: "Have a good trip." "Likewise."
senses.exampleCN: “旅途愉快。”“彼此彼此。”
senses.why: The comparison turns back on the speaker: the wish or feeling just received is returned to the sender. A whole clause is compressed into one adverb.
senses.whyCN: 比较的方向转回说话者：刚收到的祝愿或感受被原样送还给对方。整个从句被压缩成一个副词。

senses.title: Correspondence: standing in the same relation
senses.titleCN: 对应关系：处于相同的关系位置
senses.definition: in a comparison, showing that two things change or behave in a corresponding way
senses.definitionCN: 在比较中表示两件事以对应的方式变化或表现
senses.example: The two curves rise likewise during the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 两条曲线在第一季度以相同的方式上升。
senses.why: Here the shared element is not the action itself but the relation: each curve behaves toward its own baseline the way the other does toward its own. The same form is mapped onto two separate tracks.
senses.whyCN: 这里共享的不是动作本身，而是关系：每条曲线相对自己的基线如何变化，另一条也以同样方式相对自己的基线变化。相同的“形”被投射到两条独立的轨道上。

senses.title: Open extension: and similar things
senses.titleCN: 开放列举：以及诸如此类
senses.definition: in the phrase and likewise, used to extend a list to other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 用于 and likewise，把列举扩展到同类的其他事物
senses.example: The cupboard held flour, sugar, salt and likewise.
senses.exampleCN: 柜子里放着面粉、糖、盐以及诸如此类的东西。
senses.why: The same manner can widen from a single parallel case to an indefinite class: whatever else belongs to the same category is understood without being named.
senses.whyCN: “相同方式”可以从单个平行事例扩展到一整类：凡是属于同一范畴的东西，不必点名也自然被包括进来。

senses.title: Official parallel: the rule applies equally
senses.titleCN: 正式平行：规则同等适用于另一方
senses.definition: in formal or legal writing, used to apply the same rule, right, or duty to a second party
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或法律文本中，把同一规则、权利或义务同样施加于另一方
senses.example: The safety rules bind employees and likewise all contractors on site.
senses.exampleCN: 安全规定约束员工，也同样约束现场所有承包商。
senses.why: Official prose needs to bind two classes under one clause without repeating it. Likewise signals that the legal relation is copied exactly, which is why it is common in contracts and regulations.
senses.whyCN: 正式文本需要把两类主体绑进同一条款而不重复条文。likewise 表示这种法律关系被原样复制，因此常见于合同与规章。

senses.title: Usage boundary: affirmative parallels only
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：只接肯定性平行
senses.definition: a usage limit: likewise normally adds an affirmative parallel; in negative sentences English prefers either, neither, or nor
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：likewise 通常追加肯定性的平行项；否定句中英语更常用 either、neither 或 nor
senses.example: He did not sign the letter, and his partner did not either.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有在信上签字，他的搭档也没有。
senses.why: The word asserts that the same thing holds, not that the same thing fails to hold. Negative addition needs a negative polarity item, so 'did not likewise' sounds odd to most speakers.
senses.whyCN: 这个词断定“同样的事成立”，而不是“同样的事不成立”。否定追加需要否定极性词，因此“did not likewise”在多数母语者听来不自然。

senses.title: Register boundary: formal in casual agreement
senses.titleCN: 语体边界：日常附和时偏正式
senses.definition: a register limit: in informal speech, same here or me too is more natural than likewise, which can sound formal or stiff
senses.definitionCN: 语体限制：非正式口语中 same here 或 me too 比 likewise 更自然，后者可能显得正式或生硬
senses.example: "I'm starving." "Same here."
senses.exampleCN: “我饿坏了。”“我也是。”
senses.why: Because likewise began as a written-style parallel marker, its reciprocal use retains a polished edge. Friends usually choose a lighter phrase unless they are deliberately dry or humorous.
senses.whyCN: 由于 likewise 原本是书面风格的平行标记，它的回应用法仍带着修饰过的味道。朋友之间通常选更轻的说法，除非故意显得冷淡或幽默。

intro.en: Likewise is a Germanic compound made in English from like and wise. Dates are approximate, and the deepest Indo-European origin of like is not known.
intro.cn: likewise 是英语用 like 与 wise 构成的日耳曼语复合词。年代为大致估计；like 最深的印欧语来源并不确定。

items.en: Like goes back to Old English gelic 'similar, having the same form', a word built with the prefix ge- and the noun lic, which could mean 'body, form'.
items.cn: like 可追溯到古英语 gelic“相似的、具有相同形体的”，由前缀 ge- 与名词 lic 构成，后者可表示“身体、形体”。

items.en: The Germanic source is reconstructed as *galika-, literally 'having the same form', from *ga- 'together' plus *likam 'body, form'. The body-to-form shift is the interesting part of the story. The deeper PIE origin of *likam is source uncertain.
items.cn: 其日耳曼来源被重构为 *galika-，字面义“具有相同的形体”，由 *ga-“一起”加 *likam“身体、形体”构成。从“身体”到“形体”的转移是这段词源里值得注意的地方。*likam 更深的原始印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: Wise meaning 'manner, way, condition' is a separate Old English noun. It is related to witan 'to know', so the original sense is close to 'the way one knows or does something'.
items.cn: 表示“方式、方法、状况”的 wise 是另一个古英语名词，与 witan“知道”同源，因此其原义接近“一个人认知或做事的方式”。

items.en: The two words combine into the adverb likewise, first recorded in the late 14c. with the sense 'in like manner'. The written compound fixes a phrase that earlier appeared as like wise.
items.cn: 这两个词合成了副词 likewise，14 世纪晚期最早记录，义为“以同样的方式”。这个书面复合词凝固了早先写作 like wise 的短语。

items.en: Modern English keeps 'in the same way' and adds the discourse senses 'also' and 'moreover'. The adverb never inflects, and its reciprocal use in conversation is a later, familiar extension.
items.cn: 现代英语保留“以同样方式”，并发展出“也、此外”的语篇义。这个副词没有屈折变化；会话中的回应用法是较晚出现的、偏口语的延伸。

note.en: The first group shares the -wise shape or the like root; the second group approaches the same meaning from manner, degree, addition, and formal continuation.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -wise 词形或 like 词根；第二组从方式、程度、追加和正式递进四个角度靠近同一含义。

entries.definition: the state of being similar, or a picture that looks like someone. It keeps like but has no wise.
entries.definitionCN: 相似的状态，或看起来像某人的画像。它保留 like，但没有 wise。

entries.definition: in a different way, or in other respects. It uses the same -wise suffix but points away from sameness.
entries.definitionCN: 以不同的方式，或在其他方面。它使用同一个 -wise 后缀，却指向“不相同”。

entries.definition: in the direction in which a clock's hands move. It shows -wise as a productive suffix meaning 'in the manner or direction of'.
entries.definitionCN: 沿钟表指针移动的方向。它显示 -wise 是能产后缀，表示“以……的方式或方向”。

entries.definition: in a similar way. It is the closest synonym, but it compares two cases more openly and is less tied to a written parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 以相似的方式。它是最接近的同义词，但更 openly 比较两个事例，也不像 likewise 那样绑定书面平行结构。

entries.definition: to the same amount or degree. It measures quantity or rank, not the method by which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 以相同的数量或程度。它衡量数量或等级，而不是做某事的方法。

entries.definition: in addition; too. It adds a further item but does not claim that the two items behave in the same manner.
entries.definitionCN: 此外；也。它追加另一项，但不声称两项以相同方式表现。

entries.definition: in addition to what has been said, used to introduce a further point. It is formal and sequential, not a claim of identical manner.
entries.definitionCN: 除已说内容之外，用于引出进一步论点。它正式且表递进，不是“方式相同”的断言。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real parts like and wise, real fixed phrases, and real relatives such as otherwise and clockwise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分 like 与 wise、真实固定短语，以及 otherwise、clockwise 等真实同族词。

normal.en: like means 'having the same form'; wise means 'manner'. Put them together and you get 'in the same manner'.
normal.cn: like 表示“具有相同形体”，wise 表示“方式”。合起来就是“以相同的方式”。

normal.en: The suffix -wise is still alive in otherwise, clockwise, and lengthwise, all meaning 'in the manner or direction of'.
normal.cn: 后缀 -wise 仍活在 otherwise、clockwise、lengthwise 中，都表示“以……的方式或方向”。

normal.en: Do likewise is a fixed phrase: whatever the first person did, the second repeats.
normal.cn: do likewise 是固定短语：第一个人怎么做，第二个人就照样做。

normal.en: As a one-word reply, Likewise means 'the same to you' and returns the wish you just received.
normal.cn: 作为一词回应，Likewise 意为“你也一样”，把刚收到的祝愿原样送还。

normal.en: And likewise at the end of a list means 'and other things of the same kind'.
normal.cn: and likewise 放在列举末尾，表示“以及同类的其他东西”。

abstract.en: Imagine one seal pressed twice: the second impression is not the first object, but it carries exactly the same shape.
abstract.cn: 想象同一枚印章压两次：第二个印痕不是第一个物体，却带着完全相同的形状。

abstract.en: A mirror placed beside an action: whatever the first body does, the second repeats in its own material.
abstract.cn: 在动作旁边立一面镜子：第一个身体做什么，第二个就在自己的材料里重复什么。

abstract.en: Two parallel tracks: they are separate roads, but every turn on one is matched by a turn on the other.
abstract.cn: 两条平行轨道：它们是各自独立的道路，但一条上的每次转弯，另一条都有对应的转弯。

examples.en: The first team simplified its forms, and the second team did likewise.
examples.cn: 第一组简化了表单，第二组也照样做了。

examples.en: The vaccine protects children; likewise, it reduces transmission in adults.
examples.cn: 疫苗保护儿童；同样地，它也减少成人的传播。

examples.en: "Thanks for your help." "Likewise."
examples.cn: “谢谢你的帮助。”“彼此彼此。”

dict_mnemonic.text: “来客歪姿”——来客摆出和别人一样歪的姿势 → likewise 同样地

root: 古英语 gelic“具有相同形体”+ wise“方式”，字面义“以相同的方式”；核心是“照着同一个形状再做一遍”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of likewise, all from one compound: like supplies the same shape, wise supplies the manner, and the pair is then extended to addition, discourse, reply, correspondence, open lists, official rules, and two usage limits.
sensesIntro.cn: likewise 的九个义项都出自同一个复合词：like 提供相同的形，wise 提供方式；这一对成分随后延伸到追加、语篇、回应、对应关系、开放列举、正式规则，以及两条用法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same shape is carried over into a second act.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个形状被带进第二个行为里。

branches.en: MANNER AND CORRESPONDENCE: one method is copied, or two things occupy matching positions.
branches.cn: 方式与对应：一种做法被复制，或两件事占据相互对应的位置。

branches.en: PARALLEL APPLICATION: the same predicate is applied to a second item, a second clause, or a second legal party.
branches.cn: 平行适用：同一个说法被施加于第二项、第二句或第二个法律主体。

branches.en: RECIPROCAL REPLY: the comparison turns back and returns the wish to the speaker.
branches.cn: 回应：比较方向转回，把祝愿送还给说话者。

branches.en: OPEN CLASS: the same kind is left open, so the list can continue without naming every member.
branches.cn: 开放类别：同类范围保持开放，列举不必点出每一个成员。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: affirmative polarity and formal register limit where the adverb sounds natural.
branches.cn: 边界：肯定极性与正式语体限制了该副词听起来自然的范围。

intro.en: Likewise is a Germanic compound, not a Latin derivative. Like supplies the 'same form' and -wise is the noun 'manner' acting as the second element of a compound.
intro.cn: likewise 是日耳曼语复合词，不是拉丁语派生词。like 提供“相同形体”，-wise 则是充当复合词第二成分的名词“方式”。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate family here: like and wise are Germanic. The four entries below are the genuine Germanic relatives, including the still-productive -wise suffix and the wit family behind wise.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族词：like 与 wise 都是日耳曼语词。下面四条是真正的日耳曼同族词，包括仍有能产力的 -wise 后缀，以及 wise 背后与“知道”相关的 wit 词族。

items.meaningCN: 以同样的方式；也（like 表相同形体，-wise 表方式）
items.example: He nodded, and she did likewise.
items.exampleCN: 他点了点头，她也照样做了。

items.meaning: the quality of being similar; a portrait
items.meaningCN: 相似；相像；画像（-ness 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: There is a strong likeness between the two brothers.

items.meaningCN: 讨人喜欢的；可爱的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: She is a likeable and patient teacher.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位讨人喜欢又有耐心的老师。

items.meaningCN: 喜爱；喜好（-ing 构成情感名词）
items.example: He has a liking for old maps.
The first half of the word is this old adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的前半就是这个古老的形容词。

items.structure: Old English wise 'manner', used as a suffix
items.meaning: in the manner of; as regards
items.example: The same suffix forms clockwise and lengthwise.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 clockwise 与 lengthwise。

items.example: The noun still survives inside the suffix.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词仍活在后缀里。

items.meaning: to compare one thing to another
items.example: The critic likened the novel to a long letter.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把这部小说比作一封长信。
这个俱乐部吸引志趣相投的读者。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 相似的；同样地（a- 加 like“形体”）

latinEntries.meaning: of the same kind or place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一类的；同一地方的（源自古英语 ilca“相同”）

latinEntries.meaning: way or manner, surviving mainly in compounds
latinEntries.meaningCN: 方式；方法（主要保留在复合词中）
才智；知道的能力（与 wise 同源）

definition_zh: 目录；商品目录；一连串；编入目录
definition_en: a complete list of items arranged in order, especially goods for sale or books in a library, or to make such a list
core_image: 把东西一件件点清、按顺序列成单子
scene: 图书馆员在书架间查找一本书。 She opened the online catalog and typed the title.
sceneCN: 这里 catalog 指「目录」（第 1 个义项：图书按顺序编排的清单）；句意是她打开联机目录，输入书名。

derivatives.zh: 编目员
编目工作

senses.title: An ordered list of items
senses.definition: a list of names, goods or books put in a fixed order for reference
senses.definitionCN: 把名称、商品或书籍按固定顺序排列、供查检的清单
senses.example: The store mails a catalog before Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 商店在圣诞节前寄出商品目录。
senses.why: The Greek source meant a counting-off, so the list is first of all things named one by one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词意为逐一点数，所以目录首先是被一件件念出来的东西。

senses.title: A series of unwanted things
senses.definition: a long series of events or faults, usually unpleasant ones
senses.definitionCN: 一长串事件或过失，通常指令人不快的
senses.example: The report is a catalog of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一连串的失败记录。
senses.why: A list counts items in order, and when the items are faults the same word means a whole series of them.
senses.whyCN: 清单按顺序清点条目，当条目是过失时，同一个词就表示一整串过失。

senses.title: To list items in order
senses.definition: to arrange names or objects into an ordered list for later use
senses.definitionCN: 把名称或物品排成有序清单，以便日后查用
senses.example: They cataloged every letter in the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把档案中的每封信都编了目。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of reading the list, you make it.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是名词义的反向操作：不是读清单，而是把清单做出来。

intro.en: Catalog comes from a Greek verb meaning to count off, and it reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: catalog 来自一个意为逐一点数的希腊语动词，经拉丁语和法语进入英语。

items.en: Kata meant down or according to, and legein meant to say or count.
items.cn: 希腊语 kata 表示向下或按照，legein 表示说或点数。

items.en: Katalogos was a list or register, literally a counting off of items.
items.cn: katalogos 意为清单或名录，字面就是逐项点数。

items.en: Catalogus carried the Greek list word into the scholarly language of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 把这个希腊语清单词带入欧洲学术语言。

items.en: French catalogue spread the word through book trade and library practice.
items.cn: 法语 catalogue 通过图书贸易与图书馆实务推广该词。

items.en: English catalog first names a list of books or goods in a fixed order.
items.cn: 英语 catalog 最初指按固定顺序排列的书目或货单。

items.en: The word spreads to mail-order selling, computing and figurative lists of faults.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩展到邮购、计算机以及比喻性的过失清单。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Greek list word and its English endings, while the meaning group gathers other kinds of ordered records.
note.cn: 形近组保留希腊语清单词及英语词尾，近义组收其他有序记录。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
a person who makes a catalog
the work of listing items
a set of items written one below another
an alphabetical guide to pages in a book
entries.definitionCN: 按字母排列、指向书中页码的索引

entries.definition: a full count of goods in stock
entries.definitionCN: 对库存货物的全面清点

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek counting root, the library phrases and the American spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语点数词根、图书馆搭配以及美式拼写。

normal.en: Catalog and catalogue differ only by the ue ending, so remember one and you have both.
normal.cn: catalog 与 catalogue 只差结尾的 ue，记住一个就记住了两个。

normal.en: The Greek root legein, to say, hides in catalog just as it does in logic and dialogue.
normal.cn: 希腊语词根 legein（说）藏在 catalog 里，也藏在 logic 与 dialogue 里。

normal.en: Library catalog and product catalog put the word where it is most often seen.
normal.cn: library catalog 与 product catalog 把词放在最常见的两种场合。

normal.en: A catalog of errors turns a neutral list into a long complaint.
normal.cn: a catalog of errors 把中性的清单变成了一长串抱怨。

normal.en: American spelling drops the ue and doubles nothing in cataloging, keeping one l.
normal.cn: 美式拼写去掉 ue，cataloging 也只保留一个 l。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk reciting names one by one and ticking each off.
abstract.cn: 想象一位职员一件件念出名称，再逐一打勾。

abstract.en: Picture a fat paper catalog lying open at the toy section.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚厚的纸质目录摊开在玩具那一页。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of small drawers, each with a neat label.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排小抽屉，每格都贴着整齐的标签。

examples.en: The museum published a catalog of its paintings.
examples.cn: 博物馆出版了藏画目录。

examples.en: She ordered the shoes from a catalog.
examples.cn: 她从目录上订购了那双鞋。

examples.en: The librarian cataloged the new books in a week.
examples.cn: 图书管理员一周内给新书编好了目。

dict_mnemonic.text: catalog 可以拆成 cata 加 log：log 是记录，把东西一件件记下来，就成了目录。

root: 源自希腊语 katalogos（清单、名册），由 kata（按照）与 legein（说、点数）构成，经拉丁语 catalogus 与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Counting items aloud gives the list, the list extends to goods and books, and the same word names a series of faults.
sensesIntro.cn: 把东西逐一点数得出清单，清单扩展到商品与图书，同一个词又指一连串过失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: items named one by one and set down in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：把东西一件件念出来，按顺序记下。

branches.en: A shop catalog keeps goods in a fixed order for buyers.
branches.cn: 商店目录把商品按固定顺序排给买家看。

branches.en: A library catalog does the same for books and readers.
branches.cn: 图书馆目录对图书和读者做同样的事。

branches.en: The verb is the act of building the list.
branches.cn: 动词义就是编制这份清单的动作。

branches.en: When the listed items are faults, the list becomes a complaint.
branches.cn: 当列出的条目是过失时，清单就变成了控诉。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in whether the list is read or made.
branches.cn: 名词与动词只差在清单是被读还是被做出来。

intro.en: Catalog builds its family with -er and -ing, plus the British spelling catalogue.
intro.cn: catalog 用 -er 与 -ing 构词，另有英式拼写 catalogue。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form catalogus preserves the Greek list word almost unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 catalogus 几乎原样保留了希腊语的清单词。

items.example: The catalog is on the desk.
He cataloged the stamps by year.

items.exampleCN: 编目员核对了每个书名。

items.meaning: the same word in British English

items.exampleCN: catalogus 进入了中世纪拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: Catalogus kept the Greek meaning intact.
latinEntries.exampleCN: catalogus 完整保留了希腊语含义。

definition_zh: 每年；一年一次地；按年度计算地
definition_en: once every year, or in a way that is calculated over each year
core_image: 日历上被圈起来的同一个月份
scene: 董事会固定在三月碰头，桌上摆着去年的账本。 The committee meets annually in March.
sceneCN: 这里 annually 是「每年一次地」（第 1 个义项：每年发生一次）；句意是委员会每年三月开会。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：每年的；全年的
名词：年金
名词：周年纪念日

senses.title: Once every year
senses.definition: at intervals of one year, of an event that repeats
senses.definitionCN: 以一年为间隔，用于重复发生的事件
senses.example: The committee meets annually in March.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每年三月开会。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective of year into an adverb of frequency, so annually answers the question how often.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示「年」的形容词变成频率副词，所以 annually 回答的是「多久一次」。

senses.title: Calculated year by year
senses.definition: in a way that is measured or revised for each year, as with figures or rates
senses.definitionCN: 以每一年为单位进行计量或调整，如数字或比率
senses.example: Interest is compounded annually, not monthly.
senses.exampleCN: 利息按年复利计算，而不是按月。
senses.why: The same adverb can mark the unit of calculation rather than the frequency of an event, since the year is both a cycle and a measure.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词也能标示计算单位而不只是事件频率，因为年既是周期也是量度单位。

intro.en: Annually is the adjective annual with -ly added, and the year root stays visible.
intro.cn: annually 是形容词 annual 加 -ly 构成，表示「年」的词根仍然清晰。

items.en: annus meant 'year'.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」。

items.en: annualis meant 'yearly'.
items.cn: annualis 意为「每年的」。

items.en: English borrowed annual as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语借入 annual，兼作形容词与名词。

items.en: The adverb annually was formed with the native suffix -ly.
items.cn: 副词 annually 由本族语词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: Annually now also marks yearly calculation in finance and statistics.
items.cn: 现代 annually 还用于金融与统计中的按年计算。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the year root; the near-meaning group is other frequency adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组共享「年」词根；近义组是其他频率副词。

entries.definition: yearly
a yearly remembered date
a yearly payment
once a year
once a month
year after year, without stopping

normalIntro.en: Annual plus -ly gives the adverb of frequency.
normalIntro.cn: annual 加 -ly 构成频率副词。

normal.en: Annual is the adjective; add -ly for the adverb.
normal.cn: annual 是形容词，加 -ly 得到副词。

normal.en: Annually answers how often, not how long.
normal.cn: annually 回答「多久一次」，不回答「持续多久」。

normal.en: Meets annually, held annually, published annually are common.
normal.cn: meets annually、held annually、published annually 都很常见。

normal.en: Do not confuse annually with annally; the u is needed.
normal.cn: 不要漏掉 u，写成 annally 是错的。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-nu-al-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-nu-al-ly。

abstract.en: See the same date circled again on a wall calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上日历同一个日期又被圈起来。

abstract.en: See a clock whose hand takes a whole year to return.
abstract.cn: 想象一根要走一整年才回到原位的指针。

abstract.en: See a ledger reopened each January.
abstract.cn: 想象每年一月重新翻开的账本。

examples.en: The committee meets annually in March.
examples.cn: 委员会每年三月开会。

examples.en: Interest is compounded annually, not monthly.
examples.cn: 利息按年复利计算，而不是按月。

examples.en: The survey is carried out annually across the country.
examples.cn: 这项调查每年在全国范围内进行一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: annual（每年的）加 -ly（……地）：每年一次地。

root: 由形容词 annual 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；annual 来自拉丁语 annualis，词根 annus 意为「年」，与 anniversary、annuity 同族。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is frequency, the other is the unit of calculation.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项表示频率，另一个义项表示计算单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle that closes once every twelve months.
core.cn: 核心意象：每十二个月闭合一次的圆圈。

branches.en: meets annually
branches.cn: 每年开会

branches.en: held annually
branches.cn: 每年举行

branches.en: published annually
branches.cn: 每年出版

branches.en: compounded annually
branches.cn: 按年复利计算

branches.en: reported annually
branches.cn: 每年上报

intro.en: A regular -ly adverb of frequency built on the Latin adjective for year.
intro.cn: 这是一个规则的频率副词，建立在表示「年」的拉丁形容词之上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin year root annus sits inside annual and annually.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根 annus「年」藏在 annual 与 annually 之中。

definition_zh: 小路；踪迹；尾迹；（作动词）拖；跟随；落后
definition_en: a rough path through open country, or the marks left by something moving, and to drag or follow behind
core_image: 一条在草丛中被踩出来的细线，一路通向山口
scene: 山脚的草地上有一条被走过的细线，弯弯地通到松林深处。 We followed a narrow trail up through the pines to the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里 trail 是「小路」（第 1 个义项：原野中走出来的粗糙小道）；句意为我们沿着一条窄窄的小路穿过松林走到山脊。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「拖车；预告片」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「拖着的；尾随的」

senses.title: A rough path through the country
senses.definition: a narrow path worn through a wild or open area, often used for walking
senses.definitionCN: 在荒野或旷野中被踩出的窄道，多供步行
senses.example: The trail climbs steeply after the second bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了第二座桥，小路就开始陡峭地上升。
senses.why: The Latin root is a drag or a pull, so a trail is a line dragged through the grass by feet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为拖、拉，所以小路就是脚步在草上拖出的一条线。

senses.title: Marks left by a moving thing
senses.definition: the prints, scent, or signs left behind by a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物身后留下的印迹、气味或迹象
senses.example: The dogs found the trail again at the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 狗在溪边又找到了那股踪迹。
senses.why: What is dragged along leaves a mark, so the mark itself takes the name of the dragging.
senses.whyCN: 被拖着的东西会留下印记，于是印记本身也沿用了「拖」这个名字。

senses.title: Something dragging behind
senses.definition: a long part of something, such as a dress or smoke, that hangs or stretches behind
senses.definitionCN: 衣裙、烟雾等长长拖在后面的部分
senses.example: The bride's dress had a long lace trail.
senses.exampleCN: 新娘的礼服拖着长长的蕾丝尾。
senses.why: The physical act of dragging becomes the very thing that is dragged along behind.
senses.whyCN: 拖这个动作本身就变成了被拖在后面的那样东西。

senses.title: To drag along the ground
senses.definition: to let something hang down and be pulled along behind one
senses.definitionCN: 让某物垂下并被拉着在身后移动
senses.example: The child trailed a stick through the dust.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子拖着一根棍子在土里划过去。
senses.why: This is the literal source of every other sense, acted out by hand.
senses.whyCN: 这是其他所有义项的字面来源，用动作直接演示出来。

senses.title: To follow behind someone
senses.definition: to walk or move slowly behind another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 在别人或别物后面慢慢走或移动
senses.example: The little boy trailed his mother across the market.
senses.exampleCN: 小男孩跟在母亲身后穿过集市。
senses.why: If something is dragged behind you, it follows you, and a person can follow in the same manner.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西被你拖在身后，它就跟着你，人也可以以同样的方式跟随。

senses.title: To be losing in a contest
senses.definition: to be behind a competitor in score, speed, or progress
senses.definitionCN: 在比分、速度或进度上落在对手后面
senses.example: Our team trailed by two goals at half time.
senses.exampleCN: 半场时我们队落后两球。
senses.why: To be behind in space becomes to be behind in score, since contests are pictured as races along a track.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的在后成为比分上的落后，因为竞赛被想象成轨道上的赛跑。

intro.en: Trail comes through Old French traillier, to drag, from Latin tragula, a small dragnet or sled, related to trahere, to pull.
intro.cn: trail 经古法语 traillier（拖）而来，源自拉丁语 tragula（小拖网、拖橇），并与 trahere（拉）相关。

items.en: Tragula is a dragnet or sled that is hauled along the ground behind a person or animal.
items.cn: tragula 是被拖着在地上移动的拖网或拖橇。

items.en: Old French traillier means to drag along, to haul, or to draw a net.
items.cn: 古法语 traillier 意为沿地拖、拉或拖网。

items.en: English takes the verb trail for dragging, and soon uses the noun for the line left behind.
items.cn: 英语借入动词 trail 表示拖，很快又用名词指身后留下的线。

items.en: In the North American forests trail becomes the usual word for a walking path.
items.cn: 在北美的森林里，trail 成为步道的常用词。

items.en: The sense of being behind in a contest develops in the nineteenth century with organised sport.
items.cn: 竞赛中落后的含义在十九世纪随着有组织的体育运动发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the trail family and pulling relatives, while the near-meaning group gathers paths and marks of passage.
note.cn: 形近组收集 trail 词族与拖拽相关的词，近义组收集路径与经过的印记。

entries.definition: a path or the marks on it
a mark left behind
a vehicle pulled behind another
hanging or moving behind
a way along which people walk
a mark left by a foot
to go after someone

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the dragging root, from the compound habits, and from the picture of a line in the grass.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「拖」这个词根、复合搭配以及草丛里的那条线入手。

normal.en: Tragula is a dragnet pulled along the ground, so trail is always about dragging.
normal.cn: tragula 是被拖着走的拖网，所以 trail 始终围绕「拖」。

normal.en: Trail behind, on the trail of, blaze a trail: the word covers following, tracking, and pioneering.
normal.cn: trail behind、on the trail of、blaze a trail，分别覆盖落后、追踪、开创。

normal.en: Drag something and it follows, which is why the same word means both pull and follow.
normal.cn: 把东西一拖，它就跟着走，这就是同一个词既指拖又指跟的原因。

normal.en: A trailer is a thing towed behind, and a film trailer drags you into the cinema.
normal.cn: trailer 是被拖在后面的车，而电影预告片则是把你「拖」进影院。

normal.en: Trail and track are cousins: one is dragged, the other is cut.
normal.cn: trail 与 track 是表亲：一个是拖出来的，一个是刻出来的。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line pressed into tall grass, the only sign that anyone passed.
abstract.cn: 想象长草里被压出的一条细线，是有人经过的唯一证据。

abstract.en: Think of a scarf pulled along the ground and slowly collecting dust.
abstract.cn: 想一条被拖着走的围巾，慢慢沾满尘土。

abstract.en: A trail is the ground remembering a path.
abstract.cn: 小路是土地对走过的路的记忆。

examples.en: The trail leads down to a small lake.
examples.cn: 这条小路通向一个小湖。

examples.en: Police are on the trail of the missing car.
examples.cn: 警方正在追踪那辆失踪的车。

examples.en: She trailed a scarf along the railing as she walked.
examples.cn: 她一边走一边让围巾沿着栏杆拖过去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「追噢」——追着脚印往前噢，脚下踩出的就是小路。

root: 拉丁语 tragula（拖网、拖橇，与 trahere「拉」相关）→ 古法语 traillier（拖）→ 中古英语 trail。词族有 trailer、trailing。

sensesIntro.en: Everything begins with dragging: the drag leaves a line in the grass, that line becomes a path, the line behind a thing becomes its marks or its hanging end, and a follower can drag behind in a race.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都从「拖」开始：拖动在草上留下一条线，这条线成为小路，身后那条线成为踪迹或垂下的尾，而跟随者也会在竞赛中拖在后面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something pulled along the ground leaving a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被沿地拖动，留下一条线。

branches.en: The path formed by the dragging.
branches.cn: 被拖出的路。

branches.en: The marks left behind.
branches.cn: 身后留下的印记。

branches.en: The part that hangs and trails.
branches.cn: 垂下来拖着的部分。

branches.en: The act of dragging and of following.
branches.cn: 拖与跟随两个动作。

branches.en: The following that becomes losing.
branches.cn: 跟随变成落后。

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing from a Latin dragnet, with no productive suffix, and its family uses -er and -ing.
intro.cn: 本词是经法语借入的拉丁「拖网」词，没有能产后缀，其词族用 -er 与 -ing。

latinIntro.en: The Latin dragnet and the pulling verb behind it are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 下面列出这一族的拉丁「拖网」以及它背后的「拉」动词。

items.example: The stem survives in trail and trailer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干留在 trail 与 trailer 里。

items.meaning: one that does, or a thing that
items.meaningCN: 做某事者；用于某事的物

items.example: Trailing is the act of dragging behind.
Trails is plural and verb form.
items.exampleCN: trails 既是复数也是动词形式。

items.meaning: to mark trees on a new path
items.example: To blaze a trail is to open the way.
items.exampleCN: blaze a trail 就是开出一条路。

items.example: A walking trail is for foot travel.
A foot trail is the narrowest kind.
items.exampleCN: foot trail 是最窄的一种。

items.example: A snow trail is marked for skiers.
items.exampleCN: 雪道是给滑雪者标出的。

definition_zh: 公开地；当众；公然地；由公众（出资或所有）
definition_en: in a way that many people can see or hear; openly and without hiding anything; by the state or by the public as a whole
core_image: 一个人站到台上，把手里那张纸举过头顶，让全场都看得见
scene: 会场原本嘈杂，主持人走上台，请大家安静下来。 She publicly apologized to the staff she had blamed the week before.
sceneCN: 这里 publicly 是「当众、公开地」（第 1 个义项：在别人看得见听得见的地方做某事）；句意为她当众向自己上周错怪的员工道歉。图中可辨识物件：台子、话筒、举起的一页纸。

pos.zh: 公开地；当众；公然地；由公众出资或所有

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「公共的；公开的」
同族名词，义为「宣传；曝光度」
同源动词，义为「出版；发表」
同族动词，义为「宣传；使公开」

senses.title: In front of other people
senses.definition: in a place or way where other people can see and hear what is done
senses.definitionCN: 在别人看得见、听得见的地方或以这样的方式
senses.example: He publicly thanked the nurses who had saved him.
senses.exampleCN: 他当众感谢了救过他的护士们。
senses.why: Publicly is public plus -ly, so it describes an act done in the open, where the public can witness it.
senses.whyCN: publicly 是 public 加 -ly，所以它描述的是在开放场合做出、公众能够目睹的动作。

senses.title: Openly, without hiding anything
senses.definition: in an open way that conceals nothing, even when the truth is uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 以不隐瞒任何东西的开放方式，即使真相令人难堪
senses.example: The company publicly admitted that the safety test had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司公开承认那次安全测试没有通过。
senses.why: What is done before everyone cannot easily be denied afterwards, so the adverb also carries the force of refusing to conceal.
senses.whyCN: 当着所有人的面做的事，事后难以否认，所以这个副词也带着「拒绝隐瞒」的力度。

senses.title: By the state or by the public as a whole
senses.definition: by the government, or with money and ownership that belong to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 由政府，或以属于所有人的资金与所有权
senses.example: The library is publicly funded but privately run.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆由公共资金资助，却由私人运营。
senses.why: Because public also means belonging to the people, the adverb can mark who pays for or owns something rather than who watches it.
senses.whyCN: 因为 public 也指「属于人民的」，这个副词就能标明某事由谁出资、归谁所有，而不只是由谁观看。

senses.title: In a form open to everyone
senses.titleCN: 向公众开放地；可公开获取地
senses.definition: in a form that anyone is allowed to read, use or attend
senses.definitionCN: 以任何人都可以阅读、使用或参加的形式
senses.example: The data are publicly available on the council website.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据在市政会网站上可以公开获取。
senses.why: The same openness that lets people watch an act also lets them reach a record, so the adverb extends from visible action to accessible information.
senses.whyCN: 允许人看见某个举动的开放性，也同样允许人查到某份记录，于是这个副词从可见的行为延伸到可取用的信息。

intro.en: Publicly is the English adverb made by adding -ly to public, and public goes back through French to Latin publicus, built on populus, the people.
intro.cn: publicly 是英语在 public 后加 -ly 构成的副词，而 public 经法语上溯到拉丁 publicus，publicus 由 populus（人民）构成。

items.en: Populus meant the people as a body, and it underlies the whole family of public words.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是整个 public 词族的基础。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state, hence open to all rather than private.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」，因此是向所有人开放、而非私有的。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as public and handed it to English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语保留形容词形式 public，十五世纪把它交给英语。

items.en: English used public as adjective and, later, as a noun for the people, before any adverb existed.
items.cn: 英语先把 public 用作形容词，后来又用作指人民的名词，那时还没有副词形式。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly was added straight to public, giving publicly; the c is kept and no letter is dropped or doubled.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 直接加在 public 后得到 publicly；词尾的 c 保留，既不脱落字母也不双写。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for saying or doing something in the open.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示「公开说出或做出」的副词。

entries.definition: Open to all, or the people as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众。

entries.definition: Attention from the media, or the work of attracting it.
entries.definitionCN: 媒体关注，或争取关注的工作。

entries.definition: To issue a text so that the public may read it.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字发行出来供公众阅读。

entries.definition: To make something known to as many people as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 让尽可能多的人知道某事。

entries.definition: Without hiding anything from other people.
entries.definitionCN: 不向他人隐瞒任何事地。

entries.definition: In a way that is done in plain sight.
entries.definitionCN: 在众目睽睽之下做出地。

entries.definition: As it appears on the outside, whatever the inner state.
entries.definitionCN: 不论内心如何，表面上呈现地。

entries.definition: In an honest and direct way.

normalIntro.en: The word is simply public with the adverb ending -ly, and it keeps the adjective's sense of being open to everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 public 加副词后缀 -ly，保留了形容词「向所有人开放」的意思。

normal.en: Publicly is public plus -ly, with no letter added or dropped.
normal.cn: publicly 就是 public 加 -ly，既没有多写也没有少写字母。

normal.en: The -ly ending marks manner, so publicly answers the question how: in an open way.
normal.cn: -ly 标示方式，所以 publicly 回答的是「怎样做」：以开放的方式。

normal.en: Publicly owned and publicly funded point to the owner or the payer, not to the audience.
normal.cn: publicly owned 与 publicly funded 指向所有者和出资者，而不是观众。

normal.en: Publicly available stretches the same openness to records and data.
normal.cn: publicly available 把同一种开放性延伸到记录与数据上。

normal.en: The adverb never names the public itself; that job belongs to the noun public.
normal.cn: 这个副词从不指公众本身；那件事由名词 public 承担。

abstract.en: The word is a hand lifting a sheet above the head so that even the back row can read it.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一只手把纸举过头顶，让最后一排也读得到。

abstract.en: Openness has two faces here: being watched, and being reachable.
abstract.cn: 这里的开放性有两面：被人看见，以及被人够得着。

abstract.en: What is said publicly cannot afterwards be quietly unsaid.
abstract.cn: 公开说出口的话，事后没法悄悄地收回去。

examples.en: She publicly refused the offer at the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上当众拒绝了这个提议。

examples.en: The bridge is publicly owned and free to cross.
examples.cn: 这座桥归公众所有，过桥免费。

examples.en: The list is publicly available from next Monday.
examples.cn: 这份名单从下周一起可公开查阅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布立克力」——站到人人都立着看得见的地方去说去做，就是 publicly，公开地。

root: 拉丁语 populus（人民）→ publicus（属于人民的）→ 古法语 public → 英语 public；public 直接加副词后缀 -ly 得 publicly，义为「以公开、当众的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is doing something where everyone can see it; the senses divide into being watched, refusing to hide, being paid for by the public, and being reachable by anyone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「在人人看得见的地方做事」；义项由此分为被观看、拒绝隐瞒、由公众出资，以及人人可取用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person on a platform holding a sheet above the head so the whole hall can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在台上，把一页纸举过头顶，让整个大厅都看见。

branches.en: a speaker facing a full hall without notes
branches.cn: 面对满场听众、不拿讲稿的发言者

branches.en: an admission made with the cameras running
branches.cn: 在摄像机开着时作出的承认

branches.en: a library whose bills are paid from taxes
branches.cn: 账单由税款支付的图书馆

branches.en: a file anyone may open on a public site
branches.cn: 任何人都能在公开网站上打开的文件

branches.en: the same openness turned towards truth and towards access
branches.cn: 同一种开放，一面朝向真相，一面朝向取用

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective public, and the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、形容词 public，以及英语副词后缀 -ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 幸福；快乐；满足感
definition_en: the state of being happy, a feeling of joy, or quiet satisfaction
core_image: 一家人围坐灯下的安稳笑容
scene: 家人的陪伴给她带来幸福。 Her family's company brought her happiness.
sceneCN: 这里 happiness 是「幸福」（第 1 个义项）；句意：家人的陪伴给她带来幸福。

derivatives.zh: 快乐的；幸福的
快乐地
不快乐的

senses.title: State of joy
senses.definition: the state of being content and pleased with life
senses.definitionCN: 对生活感到满足和愉悦的状态
senses.example: Her family's company brought her happiness.
senses.exampleCN: 家人的陪伴给她带来幸福。
senses.why: A deep, lasting state is the main sense.
senses.whyCN: 深厚持久的状态，是主要义项。

senses.title: Feeling of joy
senses.definition: a feeling of great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 强烈的愉悦感
senses.example: The news filled the room with happiness.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让满屋充满快乐。
senses.why: A passing feeling of joy is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 短暂的喜悦感，是日常义项。

senses.title: Quiet satisfaction
senses.definition: a calm sense that life is good enough
senses.definitionCN: 觉得生活已经足够好的平静感受
senses.example: Small routines can bring quiet happiness.
senses.exampleCN: 小的日常能带来安静的满足感。
senses.why: Contentment is happiness without excitement.
senses.whyCN: 满足，是没有兴奋的幸福感。

intro.en: Happiness is happy plus the noun suffix -ness, with happy from hap, luck.
intro.cn: happiness 由 happy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，happy 来自 hap（运气）。

items.en: Happ meant chance or good luck.
items.cn: happ 意为偶然或好运。

items.en: Happy meant lucky or fortunate.
items.cn: happy 意为幸运的。

items.en: Happy came to mean glad or content.
items.cn: happy 转而意为高兴的、满足的。

items.en: The suffix -ness formed happiness, the state.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 构成 happiness，表示状态。

items.en: It named both joy and lasting contentment.
items.cn: 它兼指快乐与持久的满足。

note.en: Happiness is compared with look-alike words and words for joy and contentment.
note.cn: 把 happiness 与形近词以及表示喜悦与满足的词作比较。

entries.definition: feeling pleasure
in a happy way
an event
great pleasure
great pleasure
quiet satisfaction

normalIntro.en: Happiness is the state of joy, the feeling of delight, and the quiet sense that life is enough.
normalIntro.cn: happiness 是喜悦的状态、愉快的感觉，也是觉得生活已足够的平静。

normal.en: Her family's company brought her happiness.
normal.cn: 家人的陪伴给她带来幸福。

normal.en: The news filled the room with happiness.
normal.cn: 这个消息让满屋充满快乐。

normal.en: Small routines can bring quiet happiness.
normal.cn: 小的日常能带来安静的满足感。

normal.en: They found happiness in simple things.
normal.cn: 他们在简单的事物中找到幸福。

normal.en: True happiness does not depend on wealth.
normal.cn: 真正的幸福不取决于财富。

abstract.en: Happiness is not a place but a way of standing.
abstract.cn: 幸福不是一个地点，而是一种站立的姿态。

abstract.en: Joy arrives; contentment is built.
abstract.cn: 喜悦会到来，满足却要建造。

abstract.en: The word first meant luck, and still keeps a little of it.
abstract.cn: 这个词最初指运气，至今仍留着一丝。

examples.en: Her family's company brought her happiness.
examples.cn: 家人的陪伴给她带来幸福。

examples.en: The news filled the room with happiness.
examples.cn: 这个消息让满屋充满快乐。

examples.en: Small routines can bring quiet happiness.
examples.cn: 小的日常能带来安静的满足感。

dict_mnemonic.text: happiness 由 happy 加 -ness 构成，指「幸福、快乐」，也指安静的「满足感」；find happiness 是找到幸福，true happiness 是真正的幸福。

root: 由 happy（快乐的，源自 hap 运气）加名词后缀 -ness 构成；由运气带来的好状态，扩展为幸福、快乐与满足。

sensesIntro.en: Happiness means a state of joy, a feeling of pleasure, or quiet contentment.
sensesIntro.cn: happiness 指幸福的状态、快乐的感觉，或安静的满足。

core.en: A life felt to be good.
core.cn: 一种觉得生活很好的感受。

branches.en: A family sits together at night.
branches.cn: 一家人夜里围坐。

branches.en: Good news bursts into a room.
branches.cn: 好消息冲进房间。

branches.en: A cup of tea is enough.
branches.cn: 一杯茶就已足够。

branches.en: Lasting peace and sudden joy are both happiness.
branches.cn: 持久的安宁与突然的喜悦，都是幸福。

branches.en: Joy can settle into quiet satisfaction.
branches.cn: 喜悦可以沉淀为安静的满足。

intro.en: Happiness is happy plus -ness, with related comparatives and negatives.
intro.cn: happiness 由 happy 加 -ness 构成，另有比较级与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; hap comes from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，hap 来自古诺斯语。

definition_zh: 鸽子；家鸽；信鸽；傻瓜；受骗者；泥鸽靶
definition_en: a stout grey bird with a small head, common in cities and long kept for racing and for carrying messages
core_image: 广场上一群灰鸽落地，低头啄食，脚步一近就整片飞起
scene: 冬天的广场上，一位老人把面包屑撒在脚边，灰羽的鸟一只接一只落下来。 A lone pigeon walked between the benches as if it owned the square.
sceneCN: 这里是「鸽子」（第 1 个义项：泛指城市与乡间常见的鸽属鸟类）；句意为一只鸽子在长椅之间踱步，像广场归它所有。画面里是老人脚边落下的那一片灰羽。

derivatives.zh: 由 pigeon 与 hole 复合而成，本指鸽舍里的小格，引申为「分类格」以及动词「把……搁置归档」
由 pigeon 与 toe 的过去分词形式复合而成，形容脚尖向内、走路像鸽子的样子
由 pigeon 加表示场所的后缀 -ry 构成，义为「鸽舍；养鸽场」

senses.title: The bird itself
senses.definition: a plump grey bird with a small head and short legs, found in towns and in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 一种体形丰满、头小、腿短的灰色鸟，城市与乡间都常见
senses.example: A pigeon pecked at the crumbs under the fountain.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸽子在喷泉边啄食面包屑。
senses.why: Latin pipio named a young bird that cheeps, and English widened the word until it covered the whole grey species that shares our squares.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pipio 指会啾啾叫的雏鸟，英语把词义一步步放宽，直到覆盖与我们共用广场的这一整种灰鸟。

senses.title: A domesticated bird bred for messages or racing
senses.definition: a pigeon kept and trained by people, especially one bred to carry messages or to race home
senses.definitionCN: 由人饲养训练的鸽子，尤指培育来传信或竞翔归巢的个体
senses.example: He keeps a dozen pigeons on the roof and races them every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他在屋顶养了十几只鸽子，每年春天都拿它们去比赛。
senses.why: Tame the bird and it becomes useful, so the same name shifts from the species to the working bird whose homing instinct can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 把这种鸟驯养起来，它就有了用处，于是同一个名字从「这一种鸟」转到「能派上用场的鸟」，靠的正是它可信的归巢本能。

senses.title: A person who is easily fooled
senses.definition: a foolish person, or one who is easily tricked, used informally and often unkindly
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢的人，或容易上当的人，属口语用法，常带不客气的意味
senses.example: They sold him a broken watch, and he never guessed he had been the pigeon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们卖给他一块坏表，他一直没察觉自己才是那个上当的人。
senses.why: A tame bird that comes to any hand offering grain is an easy image for a person who trusts too quickly, and the metaphor hardened into slang.
senses.whyCN: 一只被驯熟的鸟，谁伸手递谷子它就过去，正好比喻轻信的人，这个比喻后来凝固成俚语里的固定说法。

senses.title: A clay disc used as a shooting target
senses.definition: a round disc of baked clay thrown into the air as a moving target for shooters
senses.definitionCN: 用黏土烧成的圆盘，抛向空中作为射击者的活动靶
senses.example: The clay pigeon burst into dust the moment the shot rang out.
senses.exampleCN: 枪声一响，泥鸽靶就炸成了粉末。
senses.why: Shooters needed a cheap stand-in for the bird, named the disc after it, and kept the whole phrase even though nothing living is involved.
senses.whyCN: 射击者需要一个廉价的替代物来代替真鸟，就用鸟名来称呼这个圆盘，于是整个说法被保留下来，尽管其中已经没有活物。

intro.en: Pigeon goes back to a Latin word for a chirping nestling, which French and then English widened until it named the adult bird.
intro.cn: pigeon 可上溯到一个表示「啾啾叫的雏鸟」的拉丁词，经法语与英语两次放宽，最后用来指成鸟。

items.en: Pipire was a verb for the cheeping of small birds; it is generally taken to imitate the sound itself, and any earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: pipire 是表示小鸟啾啾叫的动词；一般认为它模仿叫声本身，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Pipio named a young bird that cheeps, and it was used especially of nestlings and of young pigeons.
items.cn: pipio 指会啾啾叫的幼鸟，尤用于雏鸟与幼鸽。

items.en: Old French pijon meant a young pigeon and carried the word north into English usage.
items.cn: 古法语 pijon 意为幼鸽，把这个词带进了英语的使用范围。

items.en: Middle English spelled it pijon and then pigeon, and the meaning widened from the nestling to the adult bird.
items.cn: 中古英语先写作 pijon，后写作 pigeon，词义也从雏鸟放宽到成鸟。

items.en: Modern English adds the racing and message-carrying compounds, the clay target of shooting grounds, and the informal sense of a person easily fooled.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上竞翔与传信的复合词、射击场上的泥靶，以及「易受骗的人」这一口语义。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds and near-identical spellings around the bird; the second gathers other birds and words for a person who is easily deceived.
note.cn: 第一组收围绕这种鸟的复合词与拼写极近的词；第二组收其他鸟类，以及表示易受骗之人的词。

entries.definition: A small compartment in a desk or a rack, and by extension the act of filing something away for later.
entries.definitionCN: 书桌或架子上的小格子，引申为把某事归档、搁置起来。

entries.definition: Walking with the feet turned inward, in the way the bird's legs are set.
entries.definitionCN: 走路时脚尖向内，如同这种鸟的腿势。

entries.definition: Colouring matter used in paint or ink; it only looks similar and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 用于颜料或墨水的着色物质；只是拼写相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: A contact language with a reduced grammar, used between speakers of different tongues; it sounds the same but is a separate word of uncertain origin.
entries.definitionCN: 语法简化的接触语言，供不同语言使用者交流；读音相同，却是另一个词，来历另有说法。

entries.definition: A stockier bird of the same family, often white and used as a symbol of peace.
entries.definitionCN: 同科中体形更敦实的鸟，常为白色，被用作和平的象征。

entries.definition: A small brown city bird that also gathers wherever people scatter food.
entries.definitionCN: 城市里常见的小型褐色鸟，也会聚在有人撒食的地方。

entries.definition: A person who is easily deceived or used by others.
entries.definitionCN: 容易被欺骗、被他人利用的人。

entries.definition: The disc thrown into the air for shooting practice, whether or not the bird name is used.
entries.definitionCN: 为射击练习抛向空中的圆盘，用不用鸟名来称呼都可以。

normalIntro.en: A chirping nestling, a French diminutive and a set of English compounds carry the bird from the dovecote to the shooting range and to slang.
normalIntro.cn: 一个啾啾叫的雏鸟、一个法语指小形式，再加一串英语复合词，把这种鸟从鸽舍一路带到射击场，也带进了俚语。

normal.en: Pipio in Latin was a chirping young bird, so the word began as a description of a sound rather than the name of a species.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pipio 指会叫的幼鸟，所以这个词最初描述的是声音，而不是某一物种的名称。

normal.en: Old French kept the soft j, and English first wrote pijon before settling on pigeon.
normal.cn: 古法语保留了这个软音 j，英语先写作 pijon，后来才定为 pigeon。

normal.en: Pigeonhole started as a nesting niche in a dovecote and now names any small compartment and the act of filing something away.
normal.cn: pigeonhole 本是鸽舍里的巢格，如今指任何小格子，也指把东西归档搁置的动作。

normal.en: Carrier pigeon and homing pigeon are fixed compounds; the bird's real talent is returning home, not delivering letters by itself.
normal.cn: 信鸽与归巢鸽都是固定的复合说法；这种鸟真正的本事是认路回家，而不是自己送信。

normal.en: Pigeon-toed compares a person's turned-in feet to the bird's gait and is usually mildly mocking.
normal.cn: pigeon-toed 把人的内八字脚比作这种鸟的步态，通常带点取笑的意味。

abstract.en: A bird that lives on stone: the pigeon is the animal that turned a city into a cliff.
abstract.cn: 一只靠石头过日子的鸟：鸽子是把城市当成悬崖的那种动物。

abstract.en: The same word names the bird and the person who is fooled, as if tameness of body and trust of mind were one quality.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指这种鸟，也指上当的人，仿佛身体的驯服与心里的轻信是同一种品质。

abstract.en: Clay pigeons are named for what they are not: the target copies the flight, never the body.
abstract.cn: 泥鸽靶是用它「不是」的东西命名的：靶子复制的是飞行，从来不是身体。

examples.en: A grey pigeon pecked at the crumbs near the fountain.
examples.cn: 一只灰鸽在喷泉边啄食面包屑。

examples.en: He keeps a dozen pigeons on the roof and races them each spring.
examples.cn: 他在屋顶养了十几只鸽子，每年春天都拿它们比赛。

examples.en: The clay pigeon burst into dust as soon as the shot rang out.
examples.cn: 枪声一响，泥鸽靶就炸成了粉末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮紧」——鸽子落在肩上，皮紧了一下才发觉；pigeon 就是鸽子。

root: 拉丁语 pipio（会啾啾叫的幼鸟，源自拟声动词 pipire，更早来源不确定）经古法语 pijon 进入英语；同族词多与这种鸟及其驯养用途有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a cheeping nestling, widens to the grey bird of the square, then narrows again to the trained bird, the fooled person and the clay disc.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一只啾啾叫的雏鸟开始，放宽到广场上的灰鸟，又收窄到被驯养的鸟、上当的人，以及那个黏土圆盘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flock of grey birds dropping onto a square, pecking, then lifting as one when a step comes too near.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上一群灰鸽落地啄食，脚步一近就整片飞起。

branches.en: crumbs scattered beside a park bench
branches.cn: 长椅边撒开的面包屑

branches.en: a rooftop loft with a wire door
branches.cn: 屋顶上装着铁丝门的鸽舍

branches.en: a man counting coins for a watch that does not work
branches.cn: 有人为一块坏表数出硬币

branches.en: a clay disc spinning against the sky
branches.cn: 一只黏土圆盘在天空下旋转

branches.en: a tame bird and a trusting man, both easy to catch
branches.cn: 驯熟的鸟与轻信的人，都好捉

intro.en: An imitative Latin verb, its noun for a nestling, a French form and a set of English compounds hold the word together.
intro.cn: 一个拟声的拉丁动词、由它而来的雏鸟名词、一个法语词形和一串英语复合词，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: Only the verb of chirping and its noun are Latin; the bird's modern English name was shaped in French before English took it over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了那个拟声动词和它的名词；这种鸟的现代英语名称是先在法语里成形，再由英语接手的。

items.meaning: a small compartment, a filing slot
a pigeon bred to return home
a clay disc used as a shooting target
items.meaningCN: 用作射击靶的黏土圆盘

definition_zh: 果冻；胶状物；肉冻；果酱（美式）
definition_en: a soft, clear, sweet food that shakes, or any substance with a soft, thick, semi-solid texture
core_image: 一盘果冻轻轻一晃，整块都在颤，却没散开
scene: 孩子用勺子碰了碰盘子里的果冻，整块晃动起来。 The jelly wobbled on the plate as the table shook.
sceneCN: 这里 jelly 是「果冻」（第 1 个义项：柔软透明、会晃动的甜食），句意为桌子一震动，盘子里的果冻就晃起来。画面里的物件：盘子、勺子、果冻。

derivatives.zh: 由 jelly 加 -ed 构成，义为「冻状的；结成果冻的」
由 jelly 与 like 复合，义为「果冻状的」
由 jelly 与 fish 复合，义为「水母」

senses.title: A wobbly sweet food
senses.definition: a soft, transparent sweet food made from fruit juice and gelatine or a similar setting agent
senses.definitionCN: 用果汁加明胶或类似凝固剂做成、柔软透明的甜食
senses.example: The children ate jelly with cream.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们吃了加奶油的果冻。
senses.why: The food sense is the central one and the base of all the images that follow.
senses.whyCN: 食物义是核心，也是后面所有意象的底本。

senses.title: Any soft set substance
senses.definition: a substance that is soft, thick, and partly solid, holding its shape only loosely
senses.definitionCN: 柔软、浓稠、半固体的物质，只能勉强保持形状
senses.example: The medicine comes as a clear jelly in a tube.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药是装在软管里的透明凝胶。
senses.why: The texture, not the fruit, is what the word names here, so it spreads to gels.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的不是水果而是质地，于是词义扩展到各种凝胶。

senses.title: Meat set in its juices
senses.definition: meat cooked and cooled in its own juices until it forms a firm mass
senses.definitionCN: 肉在自身汤汁中煮熟冷却后凝成的一块
senses.example: Sunday lunch ended with cold tongue in jelly.
senses.exampleCN: 周日的午餐以舌头肉冻收尾。
senses.why: Meat set in aspic uses the same setting action as fruit jelly, so the name carried over.
senses.whyCN: 肉冻与水果冻用的是同一种凝固定型，名字就随之搬了过来。

senses.title: A fruit spread in America
senses.definition: in American English, a clear fruit spread similar to jam but smoother
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语里指比果酱更细腻透明的果摊
senses.example: He put grape jelly on his toast.
senses.exampleCN: 他在吐司上抹了葡萄酱。
senses.why: American usage keeps a separate name for the clear kind, while British usage does not.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法给透明的这种留了单独的称呼，英式则不然。

senses.title: A body weakened by fear
senses.definition: used in phrases to say that legs or nerves have gone weak and soft
senses.definitionCN: 用于说法中表示腿或神经变得发软无力
senses.example: His legs turned to jelly before the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲前他的腿都软了。
senses.why: The metaphor map is direct: something firm changes into something that shakes.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很直接：原本坚硬的东西变成了会晃的东西。

intro.en: Jelly came through Old French gelee from Latin gelata, "frozen, congealed", from gelare, "to freeze".
intro.cn: jelly 经古法语 gelee 来自拉丁语 gelata「冻结的、凝住的」，其动词是 gelare「使冻结」。

items.en: gelare meant to freeze or to congeal.
items.cn: gelare 意为使冻结、使凝结。

items.en: gelata was the feminine past participle, meaning frozen.
items.cn: gelata 是阴性过去分词，意为冻结的。

items.en: gelee meant a frost or a jelly made by setting liquid.
items.cn: gelee 意为霜冻，也指液体凝成的冻。

items.en: English took jelly for a food set into a soft solid.
items.cn: 英语借入 jelly，指凝成软固体的食物。

items.en: The word spread to gels, meat jellies, and even jellyfish.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到凝胶、肉冻，甚至水母。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jelly- family; the near-meaning group holds other set foods and soft substances.
note.cn: 形近组是 jelly- 词族；近义组收其他凝固食品与柔软物质。

entries.definition: Set in a jelly.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「做成冻的」。

entries.definition: A soft sea animal with a bell-shaped body.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「水母」，身体软似果冻。

entries.definition: To set into a firm mass.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「凝固」；jelly 由同一个凝固概念而来。

entries.definition: Fruit boiled with sugar into a thick spread.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「果酱」，带果肉，比 jelly 粗。

entries.definition: A bitter spread made from citrus fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「柑橘果酱」，常带皮。

entries.definition: A thick semi-solid substance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「凝胶」，多用于化妆品与药品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin verb to freeze into plates, tubes, and nervous legs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语「冻结」走到盘子、软管和发软的腿。

normal.en: Latin gelare means to freeze.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gelare 意为使冻结。

normal.en: Latin gelata meant frozen or congealed.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gelata 意为冻结的、凝住的。

normal.en: French gelee named both frost and fruit jelly.
normal.cn: 法语 gelee 既指霜冻也指果冻。

normal.en: His legs turned to jelly means he was very afraid.
normal.cn: His legs turned to jelly 意为非常害怕。

normal.en: A jellyfish is a fish made of jelly.
normal.cn: 水母就是一团果冻做成的鱼。

abstract.en: Jelly holds a shape only while nothing pushes it.
abstract.cn: 果冻只在没人推的时候才保住形状。

abstract.en: To set is to let a liquid decide to stand.
abstract.cn: 凝固就是让液体决定站起来。

abstract.en: A firm thing that starts to shake has turned to jelly.
abstract.cn: 坚硬的东西开始晃，就是变成软冻了。

examples.en: The jelly shook when the plate was moved.
examples.cn: 盘子一动，果冻就晃起来。

examples.en: She made raspberry jelly for the children.
examples.cn: 她给孩子们做了覆盆子果冻。

examples.en: His knees felt like jelly after the run.
examples.cn: 跑完之后他的膝盖软得像果冻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「结离」—— 果汁结了冻，离开盘子还会自己晃

root: 拉丁语 gelare「使冻结」→ gelata「冻结的」→ 古法语 gelee「冻；果冻」→ 中古英语 jelly。同族有 jellied、jellyfish，同源动词 jell。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a wobbly sweet food, any soft set gel, meat set in its juices, an American fruit spread, and weak legs.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：会晃的甜食、任何柔软的凝胶、肉冻、美式果酱，以及发软无力的腿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate of jelly trembling all over without falling apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘果冻整体颤动却没有散开。

branches.en: THE DESSERT: cream spooned over red jelly.
branches.cn: 甜点这条线：红色果冻上浇着奶油。

branches.en: THE TUBE: clear gel for a burn.
branches.cn: 软管这条线：治烫伤的透明凝胶。

branches.en: THE SUNDAY TABLE: cold tongue in its own juices.
branches.cn: 周日餐桌这条线：凝在汤汁里的舌头肉。

branches.en: THE TOAST: grape spread in an American kitchen.
branches.cn: 吐司这条线：美国厨房里的葡萄酱。

branches.en: THE STAGE: legs going soft before a speech.
branches.cn: 舞台这条线：演讲前发软的腿。

intro.en: Jelly is a French reshaping of a Latin participle; English compounds and endings come later.
intro.cn: jelly 是拉丁分词在法语里的改写，后面的复合与词尾是英语加的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb gelare and its participle gelata sit behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 gelare 及其分词 gelata 是整个词族的底子。

items.example: The stem of gelare and gelata.

items.exampleCN: 英语写作 jelly，而非 gelee。

definition_zh: 大部分；大量；体积；散装的
definition_en: the main or largest part of something
core_image: 仓库里成堆的麻袋
scene: 仓库的门一开，里面全是麻袋。 The bulk of the grain is stored here.
sceneCN: 这里 bulk 是「大部分」（第 1 个义项：整体中占多数的部分）；句意是大部分粮食都存在这里。

derivatives.zh: 笨重的，体积大的
笨重，体积大

senses.title: The largest part
senses.definition: the main or largest part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中占主要或最大的部分
senses.example: The bulk of the grain is stored here.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分粮食都存在这里。
senses.why: A heap seen as a whole is mostly its mass.
senses.whyCN: 把一堆东西看作整体，其中最多的就是它的主体。

senses.title: Great size or volume
senses.definition: the large size or mass of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物庞大的体积或分量
senses.example: The bulk of the ship filled the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘船庞大的船身占满了港口。
senses.why: The physical sense of a heap came before the idea of a share.
senses.whyCN: 「堆」这个具体形象早于「份额」这一抽象概念。

senses.title: Sold in large amounts
senses.definition: sold loose or in large amounts, without packing
senses.definitionCN: 散装或大批出售，没有小包装
senses.example: Rice is cheaper when bought in bulk.
senses.exampleCN: 大米大批购买时更便宜。
senses.why: Goods sold by the heap rather than the packet took the word.
senses.whyCN: 按堆而不是按包出售的货物，用了这个词。

intro.en: Bulk first meant the cargo in a ship's hold, then any great mass.
intro.cn: bulk 最初指船舱里的货物，后指任何庞大的堆积。

items.en: bulke named the cargo piled in a ship.
items.cn: bulke 指堆在船里的货物。

items.en: bulk widened to any large mass or body.
items.cn: bulk 扩展到任何大的形体或堆积。

items.en: The bulk of meant the greater part.
items.cn: the bulk of 指「大部分」。

items.en: Trade in bulk named goods sold loose.
items.cn: trade in bulk 指散装货物交易。

items.en: bulk covers the main part, great size and loose goods.
items.cn: 如今 bulk 涵盖主要部分、庞大体量与散装货物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bul- opening; the near-meaning group gives amount and size words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bul- 开头；近义组是数量与体积类的词。

entries.definition: the glass part of a lamp
a male cow
a large heavy ship or person
more than half of a group
a large amount without a clear shape
the amount of space something fills

normalIntro.en: Bulk is a heap big enough to be most of the pile.
normalIntro.cn: bulk 就是大到占去整堆大部分的那一垛。

normal.en: The bulk of the cost is the roof.
normal.cn: 费用的大部分在屋顶上。

normal.en: You buy rice in bulk to save money.
normal.cn: 大批买米能省钱。

normal.en: Bulky means hard to carry.
normal.cn: bulky 意为笨重难搬。

normal.en: A bulk carrier ships loose goods.

normal.en: Bulk buying lowers the unit price.

abstract.en: See a hull filling the whole dock.

abstract.en: See grain poured loose into a bin.

sensesIntro.en: The biggest share, the size of a heap, and goods sold loose.
sensesIntro.cn: 最大的份额、一堆东西的体积、以及散着卖的货物。

branches.cn: 大批购买

branches.cn: 散装货物

intro.en: Bulk takes -y and -iness to describe heavy size.
intro.cn: bulk 加 -y 与 -iness 可描述笨重的体积。
