latinIntro.cn: 词基来自中古英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

definition_zh: 刚刚；新近地；新鲜地
definition_en: recently, or in a new and fresh way
core_image: 刚出炉的面包还冒着热气
scene: 面包刚刚出炉，香气飘满整条街。 The bread was freshly baked, and its smell filled the street.
sceneCN: 这里 freshly 是「刚刚」（第 1 个义项）；句意：面包刚刚出炉，香气飘满整条街。

derivatives.zh: 新鲜的
新鲜

senses.title: Just now
senses.definition: very recently
senses.definitionCN: 就在不久前
senses.example: The bread was freshly baked, and its smell filled the street.
senses.exampleCN: 面包刚刚出炉，香气飘满整条街。
senses.why: This is the most common use of the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 这是该副词最常见的用法。

senses.title: Newly done
senses.definition: done or made in a new state
senses.definitionCN: 以崭新的状态完成或制作
senses.example: The room smelled of freshly cut wood.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里有一股新锯木材的气味。
senses.why: The adverb marks the newness of an action.
senses.whyCN: 该副词标记动作的崭新状态。

senses.title: In a fresh way
senses.definition: in a clean or lively manner
senses.definitionCN: 以洁净或鲜活的方式
senses.example: The salad was freshly prepared with herbs.
senses.exampleCN: 沙拉用香草新鲜拌制。
senses.why: Freshness can describe how something is presented.
senses.whyCN: 「新鲜」也能描述事物的呈现方式。

intro.en: Freshly is fresh with the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: freshly 是 fresh 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Fersc meant new or unsalted.
items.cn: fersc 意为新的或未腌制的。

items.en: Fresh also meant clean and lively.
items.cn: fresh 也表示洁净和鲜活。

items.en: The adverb freshly marked recent action.
items.cn: 副词 freshly 标记新近的动作。

items.en: It pairs with baked, picked, and painted.
items.cn: 它常与 baked、picked、painted 搭配。

items.en: It keeps the sense of straight from the source.
items.cn: 它保留了「直接来自源头」的含义。

note.en: Freshly is compared with similar-looking words and other time adverbs.
note.cn: 把 freshly 与形近词以及其他时间副词作比较。

entries.definition: new
of the body
without limits
not long ago
just done
a moment ago

normalIntro.en: Freshly marks the moment right after making or picking.
normalIntro.cn: freshly 标记做好或采摘后紧接着的那一刻。

normal.en: The bread was freshly baked, and its smell filled the street.
normal.cn: 面包刚刚出炉，香气飘满整条街。

normal.en: The room smelled of freshly cut wood.
normal.cn: 房间里有一股新锯木材的气味。

normal.en: The salad was freshly prepared with herbs.
normal.cn: 沙拉用香草新鲜拌制。

normal.en: She brought a bowl of freshly picked berries.
normal.cn: 她端来一碗刚采摘的浆果。

normal.en: The walls were freshly painted white.
normal.cn: 墙壁刚刚刷成白色。

abstract.en: Freshly is the sound of something just beginning.
abstract.cn: freshly 是事物刚刚开始的声音。

abstract.en: Newness is easiest to notice right away.
abstract.cn: 崭新在最初的一刻最容易被察觉。

abstract.en: A moment old is already a memory.
abstract.cn: 片刻之后，刚刚也成为回忆。

examples.en: The bread was freshly baked, and its smell filled the street.
examples.cn: 面包刚刚出炉，香气飘满整条街。

examples.en: She brought a bowl of freshly picked berries.
examples.cn: 她端来一碗刚采摘的浆果。

examples.en: The walls were freshly painted white.
examples.cn: 墙壁刚刚刷成白色。

dict_mnemonic.text: fresh（新鲜的）+ -ly（副词后缀）= freshly；常见搭配 freshly baked / picked / painted，表示「刚刚」。

root: 由古英语 fersc（新的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心义「以崭新状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Freshly means just now, newly done, or in a fresh way.
sensesIntro.cn: freshly 意为刚刚、新近地或新鲜地。

core.en: The moment right after something is made.
core.cn: 事物做好后紧接着的那一刻。

branches.en: Warm bread comes from the oven.
branches.cn: 温热的面包刚从炉里出来。

branches.en: The smell of new wood fills a room.
branches.cn: 新木头的气味充满房间。

branches.en: Herbs are stirred into a fresh salad.
branches.cn: 香草被拌进新鲜沙拉。

branches.en: Just made and newly done share one moment.
branches.cn: 刚刚做好与新近完成共享同一时刻。

branches.en: Newness can be smelled and tasted.
branches.cn: 崭新可以被闻到，也可以被尝到。

intro.en: Freshly shows -ly turning freshness into an adverb.
intro.cn: freshly 展示了 -ly 把「新鲜」变成副词。

latinIntro.en: Freshly is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: freshly 属日耳曼语，并非拉丁语。

items.example: Fresh flowers stood in a jar.

items.exampleCN: 她买了刚烤好的小面包。

items.example: The tea is made from freshly picked leaves.
items.exampleCN: 这茶用刚采摘的叶子制成。
刚剪下的草闻起来很甜。

items.example: Do not touch the freshly painted door.

definition_zh: 跳舞的人；舞蹈演员
definition_en: a person who dances, especially as a performer or a job
core_image: 舞台上踮起脚尖、汗珠落在地板上的舞者
scene: 灯光打下来，台上的舞者踮着脚尖停了一瞬。 The dancer held her pose under the light.
sceneCN: 这里 dancer 指「舞蹈演员」（第 1 个义项：以跳舞为业的人）；句意是灯光下那位舞者定格了一瞬。

derivatives.zh: 跳舞；舞蹈
跳舞这项活动
适合跳舞的
舞池

senses.title: A person who dances
senses.definition: someone who is dancing or who dances often
senses.definitionCN: 正在跳舞或经常跳舞的人
senses.example: She is a good dancer and never sits out a song.
senses.exampleCN: 她很会跳舞，从不坐着错过一支曲子。
senses.why: The suffix -er simply turns the act into the person doing it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 只是把动作变成了做这个动作的人。

senses.title: A performer on stage
senses.definition: a person who dances as a profession before an audience
senses.definitionCN: 以在观众面前跳舞为职业的人
senses.example: The lead dancer hurt her ankle during rehearsal.
senses.exampleCN: 领舞在排练时伤了脚踝。
senses.why: When the dancing is paid for, the person becomes a role in a company.
senses.whyCN: 当跳舞能换来报酬，这个人就成了剧团里的一个角色。

intro.en: Dancer is dance plus the agent suffix -er, modelled on the French word for one who dances.
intro.cn: dancer 由 dance 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，模仿法语中「跳舞的人」的说法。

items.en: Danceur named the person who moved to music.
items.cn: danceur 指随音乐起舞的人。

items.en: Dancer appeared as the plain English name for such a person.
items.cn: dancer 作为这种人的英语称呼出现。

items.en: The word began to mark a trade as well as an activity.
items.cn: 这个词开始既指活动，也指一门行当。

items.en: Ballet dancer named a specialist who trained for years.
items.cn: ballet dancer 指受过多年训练的专门人才。

items.en: Dancer now covers everyone from a child at a party to a star on stage.
items.cn: 如今 dancer 既指聚会上的孩子，也指舞台上的明星。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ancer or -anger ending, and the meaning group names other people who perform.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ancer 或 -anger 的结尾，近义组则列出其他登台的人。

entries.definition: to move the body in time with music
the chance that harm will come
a horse or person that steps high
a person who entertains an audience
a female ballet dancer
a person who performs difficult physical tricks
entries.definitionCN: 做高难身体动作的杂技演员

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a body that cannot keep still and end with a name printed on a poster.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一副停不下来的身体开始，落到海报上印着的名字。

normal.en: A dancer is a dance that has learned to stand up.
normal.cn: 舞者是学会了站起来的舞蹈。

normal.en: The floor knows a dancer by the worn spots.
normal.cn: 地板靠磨白的地方认出舞者。

normal.en: Counting stops being work once the dancer trusts the body.
normal.cn: 舞者一旦信任身体，数拍子就不再是苦差。

normal.en: Every dancer keeps a bruise the audience never sees.
normal.cn: 每个舞者都藏着一块观众看不见的淤青。

normal.en: Add -er to the act and you get the one who does it.
normal.cn: 给动作加上 -er，就得到做这件事的人。

abstract.en: Picture a single figure alone under a narrow light.
abstract.cn: 想象一束窄光下独自站着的一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a row of bodies moving as if joined by a string.
abstract.cn: 想象一排身体像被一根线牵着一起动。

abstract.en: Picture the moment before the music, when the room holds its breath.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐响起前的一刻，整个厅都屏住呼吸。

examples.en: The dancer held her pose under the light.
examples.cn: 那位舞者在灯光下保持着姿势。

examples.en: He is the best dancer in our class.
examples.cn: 他是我们班舞跳得最好的人。

examples.en: The dancers rehearsed until midnight.
examples.cn: 舞者们排练到半夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dancer 记成「跳舞的人」：dance 是跳，-er 是「做的人」，合起来就是跳舞的人。

root: 由 dance 加施动后缀 -er 构成，模仿法语中表示跳舞者的词形；十四世纪起指跳舞的人，十六世纪起兼指以跳舞为业者，十八世纪后又分出芭蕾这一专门行当。

sensesIntro.en: From anyone keeping time with the music, to a trained body on a stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任何跟着音乐打拍子的人，到舞台上受过训练的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body on tiptoe with sweat on the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个踮着脚尖、地板上落着汗珠的身体。

branches.en: Anyone who moves to the music earns the name at once.
branches.cn: 任何随音乐动起来的人，立刻就得到这个称呼。

branches.en: Years of training turn the same name into a profession.
branches.cn: 多年训练把同一个称呼变成一门职业。

branches.en: The amateur and the professional share one verb underneath.
branches.cn: 业余者和专业者底下共用同一个动词。

branches.en: Both senses require an audience, even if it is only one friend.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要观众，哪怕只是一位朋友。

branches.en: The profession is only the child who refused to sit down.
branches.cn: 所谓职业，不过是那个不肯坐下的孩子。

intro.en: Dancer sits at the centre of a small word family built on the verb dance.
intro.cn: dancer 站在以动词 dance 为核心的小词族中间。

latinIntro.en: The -er is Germanic in form, while the base dance came through French.
latinIntro.cn: -er 是日耳曼语形式，而词根 dance 则经法语而来。

items.example: The dancer bowed to the crowd.
The song is slow but danceable.
She became a ballet dancer at nineteen.
items.exampleCN: 她十九岁成为芭蕾舞演员。

items.meaning: the main dancer of a group
items.example: The lead dancer opened the show.
The folk dancers wore red belts.

items.meaning: a dancer who supports the main singer
items.example: Four backup dancers stood behind him.

definition_zh: 盒式磁带；暗盒；胶卷盒
definition_en: a small flat plastic case holding magnetic tape or film, used for recording sound or pictures
core_image: 一只扁平的小盒子，里面卷着长长的带子
scene: 她在阁楼里翻出一台旧录音机。 The machine still played the cassette her father had recorded.
sceneCN: 这里 cassette 指「盒式磁带」（第 1 个义项：装着磁带的扁盒）；句意是这台机器还能播放她父亲录的那盘磁带。

derivatives.zh: 微型盒式磁带
磁带卡座

senses.title: A case of magnetic tape
senses.definition: a small flat case containing magnetic tape that is played in a recorder
senses.definitionCN: 装着磁带、可放入录音机播放的扁平小盒
senses.example: He keeps his old cassettes in a shoebox.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧磁带收在一个鞋盒里。
senses.why: The core image is a little box, and magnetic tape wound inside it is the use that made the word famous.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是一只小盒子，而卷在里面的磁带正是让这个词广为人知的用途。

senses.title: A lightproof film container
senses.definition: a lightproof case that holds photographic film and fits into a camera
senses.definitionCN: 装胶卷、可装入相机的防光小盒
senses.example: Load the cassette before you close the camera.
senses.exampleCN: 合上相机前先装好胶卷暗盒。
senses.why: This is the older photographic use: the same little case protects film from light instead of tape from dust.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的摄影用法：同样的小盒子保护的是胶卷而不是磁带，防的是光而不是灰。

intro.en: Cassette is a French diminutive of a word for box, borrowed into English first for film and later for tape.
intro.cn: cassette 是法语中表示盒子的词的指小形式，英语先用它指胶卷盒，后指磁带盒。

items.en: Capsa meant a box, the same root that gives case and cash.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 意为盒子，与 case、cash 同源。

items.en: Casse was a box, and cassette a little box, with the diminutive -ette.
items.cn: 法语 casse 指盒子，加指小词尾 -ette 后 cassette 就是小盒子。

items.en: English borrowed cassette for a small ornamental box.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 cassette，指小巧的装饰盒。

items.en: Photography applied the word to the lightproof case holding film.
items.cn: 十九世纪摄影术用该词指装胶卷的防光暗盒。

items.en: The tape recorder gave the word its most common modern meaning in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪磁带录音机赋予该词今天最常见的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the little-box root, while the meaning group gathers recording media.
note.cn: 形近组沿「小盒子」词根展开，近义组收录音载体。

entries.definition: a container for holding something
a very small tape cassette
a machine for playing tapes without a radio
entries.definitionCN: 不带收音功能的磁带播放机

entries.definition: a long thin strip coated for recording sound
entries.definitionCN: 涂有磁层用于录音的长带

entries.definition: a sealed case holding film or ink
entries.definitionCN: 装有胶卷或墨水的密封盒

entries.definition: a round holder that tape or film is wound on
entries.definitionCN: 缠绕磁带或胶卷的圆盘

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-box root, the -ette ending and the everyday player phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小盒子词根、-ette 词尾以及日常播放机搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ette means little, as in cigarette and kitchenette, so a cassette is a little case.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ette 表示小，如 cigarette 和 kitchenette，所以 cassette 就是小盒子。

normal.en: Cassette and case share the Latin box root, which links the word to its shape.
normal.cn: cassette 与 case 共享拉丁语的盒子词根，这把词与外形连在一起。

normal.en: Cassette player and cassette recorder are the phrases that fix the tape sense.
normal.cn: cassette player 和 cassette recorder 是固定磁带义的搭配。

normal.en: Video cassette extends the same box to pictures as well as sound.
normal.cn: video cassette 把同一种盒子从声音扩展到画面。

normal.en: The plural cassettes simply adds an s, with no change of stress.
normal.cn: 复数 cassettes 只加一个 s，重音不变。

abstract.en: Picture a thin brown ribbon wound on two tiny wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细细的棕色带子绕在两个小轮上。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pressing a stiff flap shut on a tape.
abstract.cn: 想象手指把磁带上硬硬的盖板按合。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where film waits inside a sealed box.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里胶卷待在密封盒中等待曝光。

examples.en: The cassette jammed inside the player.
examples.cn: 磁带卡在播放机里了。

examples.en: She labelled every cassette with a date.
examples.cn: 她给每盘磁带都标了日期。

examples.en: This camera takes a small film cassette.
examples.cn: 这台相机使用小号胶卷暗盒。

dict_mnemonic.text: cassette 的词尾 -ette 表示小，可以记成「小 case」：一只装着磁带的小盒子。

root: 源自法语 cassette（小盒子），由 casse（盒子）加指小词尾 -ette 构成，更早可追到拉丁语 capsa（盒）。

sensesIntro.en: A little box first holds ornaments, then film, then magnetic tape, and each use keeps the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只小盒子先装装饰品，再装胶卷，再装磁带，每种用途都保留同一外形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flat box with something wound inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只扁平小盒，里面卷着东西。

branches.en: Magnetic tape inside the box becomes the sound-recording sense.
branches.cn: 盒里的磁带成了录音义。

branches.en: Film inside the box becomes the photographic sense.
branches.cn: 盒里的胶卷成了摄影义。

branches.en: Both senses depend on the box keeping light and dust away from a sensitive strip.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖盒子替敏感的带子挡住光和灰尘。

branches.en: Player and recorder compounds keep this sense dominant today.
branches.cn: 播放机和录音机类复合词让这个义项在今天占据主导。

branches.en: The film sense now sounds old-fashioned but stays in camera manuals.
branches.cn: 胶卷义如今显得老旧，却仍留在相机说明书里。

intro.en: Cassette builds a thin family through compounds and the diminutive ending it already carries.
intro.cn: cassette 通过复合词和它本来就带的指小词尾形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The word descends from Latin capsa, a box, through the French diminutive cassette.
latinIntro.cn: 该词经法语指小形式 cassette 上溯到拉丁语 capsa（盒子）。

items.meaning: a small tape or film case
items.example: The cassette is in the drawer.

items.exampleCN: 盒子里装了四十盘磁带。
这台磁带播放机还能用。

items.meaning: a machine that records on tapes
items.example: He bought a cheap cassette recorder.
items.exampleCN: 他买了台便宜的盒式录音机。
这台口述机用的是微型磁带。

items.meaning: a tape player without a radio

items.example: The case has a strong hinge.
items.exampleCN: 这只盒子有结实的合页。

latinEntries.example: Capsa is the deep root of cassette.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cassette 的深层词根。

latinEntries.example: French cassette added the sense of small.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 法语 cassette 加上了「小」的含义。

definition_zh: 入侵；侵略；侵犯；蜂拥而入
definition_en: the act of an army or a large number of people entering a place by force, or of something harmful spreading in
core_image: 一支队伍踏过界碑，潮水一样涌进别人的院墙
scene: 深夜的海岸线上，探照灯扫过浅滩，士兵从登陆艇上跳进水里。 The islanders still tell stories of the invasion.
sceneCN: 这里 invasion 是「入侵」（第 1 个义项：武力进入他国领土），句意为岛民至今仍在讲那次入侵的故事。画面里的物件：探照灯、登陆艇、浅滩。

pos.zh: 名词：入侵；侵略；侵犯；大量涌入

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -sion 加 -de，义为「入侵；侵犯」
由本词词根加 -ive 构成，义为「侵入的；侵袭性的」
由 invade 加 -er 构成，义为「入侵者」
同带 -sion 尾的形近词，义为「逃避；回避」

senses.title: Army crossing a border
senses.definition: the act of an army entering a country with force in order to take control of it
senses.definitionCN: 军队武力进入他国、企图控制该国的行为
senses.example: The invasion began before dawn and cut the capital off within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵在黎明前开始，一天之内就切断了首都与外界的联系。
senses.why: Latin invadere meant "to go into", built from in- plus vadere, "to go".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invadere 意为「走进去」，由 in- 加 vadere「走」构成。

senses.title: Taking something over
senses.definition: the unwanted entry of a rival power into the affairs or land of another state
senses.definitionCN: 敌对势力不受欢迎地进入他国的事务或领土
senses.example: The treaty promised aid to any member facing an invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺援助任何遭遇侵占的成员国。
senses.why: Once "go into" gained a hostile tone, the noun naturally meant a hostile entry.
senses.whyCN: 「走进去」一旦带上敌意，名词自然就指敌意的进入。

senses.title: Privacy broken into
senses.definition: an unwanted and unlawful entry into someone else's private life or space
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意且不合法地进入他人的私生活或私人空间
senses.example: Reading her letters felt like an invasion of privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 看她的信件感觉像是对隐私的侵犯。
senses.why: English extended the military noun to the borders of the self rather than of the state.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个军事名词从国家的边界挪到了个人的边界。

senses.title: A crowd or a plague
senses.definition: a large number of people or things arriving or spreading where they are not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人或事物不受欢迎地到来或蔓延
senses.example: The town is bracing for an invasion of holidaymakers in July.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇正在为七月的度假人群大批涌入做准备。
senses.why: The metaphor of a flood is old: what pours in without being asked counts as an invasion.
senses.whyCN: 「洪水」的比喻很古老：不请自来涌进来的东西都算入侵。

intro.en: Invasion comes straight from Latin invasio, a noun of "going in" onto someone else's ground.
intro.cn: invasion 直接来自拉丁语 invasio，是「走进」他人土地的名词。

items.en: The verb vadere meant "to go" and appears in many motion words.
items.cn: 动词 vadere 意为「走」，出现在许多表示移动的词中。

items.en: in- added direction to it, giving invadere, "to go into".
items.cn: in- 给它加上方向，构成 invadere「走进去」。

items.en: The noun invasio named the act of entering, often hostilely.
items.cn: 名词 invasio 指进入的行为，常带敌意。

items.en: French reshaped the noun as invasion before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语先把该名词改写成 invasion，英语再借入。

items.en: English kept the military sense and added the privacy sense in legal use.
items.cn: 英语保留军事义，又在法律用法中添了隐私义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the inva-/inve- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for hostile entry.
note.cn: 形近组共用 inva-/inve- 开头；近义组收表示敌意进入的词。

entries.definition: The act of avoiding something by trickery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「逃避」，靠花招躲开。

entries.definition: Something newly created or made up.
The act of turning something upside down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「倒置」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: A sudden violent attempt to hurt or damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「攻击」，强调突然动手。

entries.definition: A short sudden attack into enemy ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「突袭」，短促而突然。

entries.definition: An unwanted arrival into a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「闯入」，强调不受欢迎。

normalIntro.en: These hooks attach the word to border crossings you can picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你想象得出的越界画面上。

normal.en: in- means into, and vad- means go.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vad- 是「走」。

normal.en: in + vad + ion: the going into a place.
normal.cn: in + vad + ion：走进一个地方这件事。

normal.en: An invasion force is the group that does the going in.
normal.cn: 入侵部队就是负责走进去的那批人。

normal.en: Invasion is invasion only when the door was not opened.
normal.cn: 门不是自己打开的，才叫入侵。

normal.en: Its verb is invade, which drops the -sion.
normal.cn: 它的动词是 invade，少了 -sion 那一截。

abstract.en: Invasion is a border crossed without permission.
abstract.cn: 入侵就是一条未经许可被越过的边界。

abstract.en: When a crowd becomes a tide, the word comes out.
abstract.cn: 当人群变成潮水，这个词就出场了。

abstract.en: Privacy has borders too, and letters are a wall.
abstract.cn: 隐私也有边界，信件就是一堵墙。

examples.en: The museum closed when news of the invasion reached the city.
examples.cn: 入侵的消息传到城里，博物馆就关门了。

examples.en: Critics called the camera in the changing room an invasion of privacy.
examples.cn: 批评者称更衣室里的摄像头侵犯了隐私。

examples.en: Every summer brings an invasion of insects to the lake.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，湖边都会被虫子大批占据。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vas（走）+ ion（名词）——踩进别人的地界

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vadere「走」→ invasio「进入」→ 法语 invasion → 英语 invasion。同族有 invade、invasive、invader。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: an army crossing in, taking over another land, breaking into privacy, and a flood of people or things.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：军队越境进入、侵占他国、侵犯隐私，以及人潮物潮的大量涌入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary being crossed from the outside by force.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界被外力从外面跨过。

branches.en: THE LANDING: troops stepping onto a foreign shore.
branches.cn: 登陆这条线：士兵踏上一片异国的海岸。

branches.en: THE FLOOD: numbers that pour in without welcome.
branches.cn: 潮水这条线：不受欢迎地涌来的人与物。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a private space entered without leave.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：未经允许进入的私人空间。

branches.en: THE LINE: both senses break a boundary they were not invited past.
branches.cn: 界线这条线：两个义项都越过了没被邀请越过的界。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: both senses take what belongs to someone else.
branches.cn: 占夺这条线：两个义项都拿走了属于别人的东西。

intro.en: Invasion is in- "into", the root vad- "go", and the noun ending -sion.
intro.cn: invasion 是 in-「进入」、词根 vad-「走」与名词词尾 -sion 的组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere and invasio are both recorded; the past participle invasus supplied the -s-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vadere 与 invasio 均有记载，过去分词 invasus 提供了那个 -s-。

items.example: The root survives in evade and pervade.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根仍见于 evade 与 pervade。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor.
English kept the verb beside the noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把动词和名词并留着。
词尾 -er 指做这事的人。

items.meaning: to go out of the way
items.example: The same root with e- for out gives the opposite motion.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根配 e-「向外」就成了反向动作。

definition_zh: 前言；序言；引言；为……作序；以……作为开场；前奏
definition_en: the introductory part of a book, the act of writing one, and an event or remark that comes before and introduces something larger
core_image: 书页刚翻开，第一行字略小，页边留白很宽
scene: 旧书摊上那本诗集的封面已经卷边，翻开第一页，作者的字迹还很清楚。 In the preface the poet thanked the friend who had kept his early drafts.
sceneCN: 这里 preface 指「前言、序言」（第 1 个义项：正文之前由作者写的引子）；句意为诗人在序言里感谢那位替他保存早期草稿的朋友。图中可辨识物件：卷边的封面、第一页上略小的字、宽阔的页边留白。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 praefari 加形容词后缀 -ory 构成，义为「引言性的；开场的」
由 preface 加表示人的 -er 构成，义为「写序言的人」
由 preface 加 -ed 构成的过去分词作定语，义为「带有序言的」

senses.title: The introductory part of a book
senses.definition: the short section at the beginning of a book, usually written by the author to explain its aim, method or history
senses.definitionCN: 书开头的一段短文，通常由作者说明写作目的、方法或成书经过
senses.example: In the preface she explains why the study took twelve years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在前言里说明了这项研究为何花了十二年。
senses.why: Latin praefatio was a saying beforehand, and a book's opening words are exactly that: the author speaks before the argument proper begins.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praefatio 就是「预先说的话」，一本书开头那几句正是如此：作者在正文论证真正开始之前先开口。

senses.title: To write a preface for a book
senses.definition: to write or provide a short introduction for a book, usually one written by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 为一本书撰写或提供短序，通常是替别人写的
senses.example: A retired professor prefaced the new edition.
senses.exampleCN: 一位退休教授为这个新版本作了序。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without adding a single letter, because English lets the name of a thing become the act of putting that thing there.
senses.whyCN: 名词不添一个字母就变成动词，因为英语允许把一件事物的名字直接用成「把它放上去」的动作。

senses.title: Words or events that come first
senses.definition: something said or done before a larger event, serving to introduce it
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的事件之前说出或做出、起引子作用的话或事
senses.example: He prefaced his question with a long account of his own week.
senses.exampleCN: 他先讲了一大段自己这一周的经历，才把问题提出来。
senses.why: Anything that speaks before the main thing can be called a preface, so the word leaves the book and comes to name a conversational or historical opening.
senses.whyCN: 凡是抢在正事之前开口的东西都能叫 preface，于是这个词离开书本，转而指谈话或历史事件的开场。

intro.en: Preface goes back to a Latin verb of solemn speech: prae- before plus fari to speak, so the word has always meant words placed in front of other words.
intro.cn: preface 可追溯到拉丁语里表示郑重说话的动词：prae-（在前）加 fari（说），所以这个词一直指放在别的话前面的那段话。

items.en: Fari meant to speak or to utter, and it was an old religious and legal verb for saying something with weight.
items.cn: fari 意为说话、说出，是一个古老的宗教与法律用语，指有分量地讲出某事。

items.en: Prae- meant before, in place as well as in time, and it is the same prefix found in predict and prevent.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前」，空间和时间都可用，predict 与 prevent 里也是这个前缀。

items.en: Praefari meant to say something first, especially a formula spoken before a rite or a formal speech.
items.cn: praefari 意为先说出某话，尤指仪式或正式演讲之前先念的套语。

items.en: The noun praefatio named that preliminary saying, and later the written introduction placed before a work.
items.cn: 名词 praefatio 指这番预先的开场话，后来又指放在作品前面的书面引言。

items.en: English took the word through Old French preface, first for a spoken opening and soon for the opening pages of a book.
items.cn: 英语经古法语 preface 借入这个词，先指口头的开场，很快又指一本书开头的几页。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the word's own relatives beside two near-spellings from other Latin stems; the near-meaning group gathers names for the parts placed before a main text.
note.cn: 形近组把本词自己的同族词与两个来自其他拉丁词干的近形词放在一起；近义组收「放在正文之前那部分」的各种名称。

entries.definition: Serving as an introduction, especially at the start of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 起引言作用的，尤指书前的。

entries.definition: Having a preface, or introduced by one.
entries.definitionCN: 带有序言的；由序言开头的。

entries.definition: An official in charge of a district or a school; from Latin praefectus, a different stem, so the likeness is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 负责一个地区或学校的官员；出自拉丁语 praefectus，词干不同，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A group of letters added to the front of a word; it shares prae- but not fari, so the likeness is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 加在词首的一组字母；它与本词共用 prae-，但并非出自 fari，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A short introduction to a book, usually written by someone other than the author.
entries.definitionCN: 书前的短序，通常由作者以外的人撰写。

entries.definition: The opening part of a book that sets out its subject and purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 书的开头部分，用来说明主题与目的。

entries.definition: The opening section of a play or long poem, spoken before the main action.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧或长诗开篇、在正戏之前说出的部分；开场白。

entries.definition: An introductory statement placed before a speech, a law or an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 演讲、法律或协议之前的引言。

normalIntro.en: The word is two Latin pieces and nothing else: before plus speak. Every sense keeps that order, words set in front of other words.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是两块拉丁部件，没有别的：在前 加 说。每个义项都守着这个次序，把话放在别的话前面。

normal.en: Prae- is before and fari is to speak, so a preface is literally the speaking that comes first.
normal.cn: prae- 是在前，fari 是说，所以 preface 字面就是「最先说的那番话」。

normal.en: A preface is usually the author's own; a foreword is usually someone else's, which is why both exist.
normal.cn: preface 通常是作者自己写的，foreword 通常由别人写，两个词因此并存。

normal.en: Prefatory adds -ory and means of the nature of an introduction, as in a prefatory note.
normal.cn: prefatory 加 -ory，意为「引言性质的」，如 prefatory note（引言性说明）。

normal.en: Preface the book with a quotation turns the noun into a verb of arranging what comes first.
normal.cn: 把名词用作动词说「以一句引文为这本书作序」，讲的就是安排什么排在前面。

normal.en: Prefaced by applause describes a speech, and the picture is still an opening placed in front.
normal.cn: prefaced by applause 形容一场演讲，画面仍然是「放在前面的开场」。

abstract.en: A preface is a doorway built out of words: you pass through it before you enter the book.
abstract.cn: 序言是用话搭出来的一道门：进书之前先穿过它。

abstract.en: The word treats every beginning as a smaller thing standing in front of a larger one.
abstract.cn: 这个词把每个开端都看成一个小东西，立在一个更大的东西前面。

abstract.en: Because prae- is shared with predict, both words are about speaking ahead; only one speaks about the book and one about the future.
abstract.cn: 因为与 predict 共用 prae-，两个词都关于「提前说」；只是一个说书，一个说未来。

examples.en: In the preface she explains why the study took twelve years.
examples.cn: 她在前言里说明了这项研究为何花了十二年。

examples.en: A retired professor prefaced the new edition.
examples.cn: 一位退休教授为这个新版本作了序。

examples.en: He prefaced his question with a long account of his week.
examples.cn: 他先讲了一大段自己这一周的经历，才提出问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞法斯」——翻开书先「预先说法」；preface 就是前言，也能当动词表示作序。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ fari（说）→ praefari（先说）→ praefatio（开场话、引言）→ 古法语 preface → 英语 preface。同族有 prefatory。

sensesIntro.en: The senses keep one position: in front. Words in front of a book, the act of putting them there, and any remark or event that opens something larger.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项守着同一个位置：在前面。放在书前的话、把话放到书前的动作，以及为更大事件开场的话或事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book opened at the first page, its type a little smaller, the margin left wide.
core.cn: 核心意象：书翻到第一页，字略小一些，页边留出很宽的空白。

branches.en: a first page whose type is smaller than the rest
branches.cn: 第一页字号比正文小的书

branches.en: a pen signing the name under a short opening note
branches.cn: 在简短开场白下签名的笔

branches.en: a long story told before the real question
branches.cn: 在真正的问题之前讲的一大段

branches.en: an opening note and an opening remark, both placed first
branches.cn: 一段书前的话与一段开场的话，都放在最前

branches.en: an editor asking a senior scholar for a few pages
branches.cn: 编辑请一位老学者写几页序

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, before and speak, make the noun; English then adds -ed and -er, while the older Latin adjective survives as prefatory.
intro.cn: 两块拉丁部件「在前」与「说」造出名词；英语再加 -ed 与 -er，而更早的拉丁形容词则以 prefatory 的形式留存。

latinIntro.en: Fari, praefari and praefatio are recorded Latin forms, and the adjective prefatory keeps the Latin suffix -ory; nothing here needs reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: fari、praefari 与 praefatio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，形容词 prefatory 还保留着拉丁后缀 -ory；这里没有需要重构的部分。

items.meaning: the opening section of a book

definition_zh: 船、舰；容器、器皿；（体内的）血管、导管
definition_en: a ship or large boat, a hollow container for liquid, or a tube that carries blood or other fluid in the body
core_image: 一个中空的器皿，能装水，也能载人渡海
scene: 港湾里停着一艘旧货船，甲板上的木桶正被吊下船。 A small vessel carried the crew back to the shore at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 vessel 是「船、舰」（第 1 个义项：水上交通运输工具）；句意为黄昏时一艘小船把船员送回岸边。水上能载人的那个容器，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：船、舰；容器、器皿；血管、导管

derivatives.zh: 加 -ed 构成，义为「有容器的；装了器皿的」（罕见）
同一拉丁词源 vas 的后代，义为「花瓶」
拉丁语原词，义为「容器」，是解剖学 vas deferens 的第一部分

senses.title: A ship or large boat
senses.titleCN: 船、舰：水上往来的大型运载工具
senses.definition: a ship or large boat, especially one used for trade or war
senses.definitionCN: 船或大型艇，尤指用于贸易或军事的
senses.example: A cargo vessel left the port before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，一艘货船就离港了。
senses.why: Latin vas means a container; a ship is the container people live in while crossing water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vas 意为「容器」；船就是人们渡水时居住其中的那个容器。

senses.title: A container for liquid
senses.definition: a hollow container, especially one used for holding liquids
senses.definitionCN: 中空的容器，尤指盛放液体的器皿
senses.example: The priest poured oil from a clay vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 祭司从一个陶器里倒出油。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: something hollow that holds what is put inside.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：中空之物，把放进去的东西盛住。

senses.title: A tube in the body
senses.titleCN: 血管、导管：体内的输送管道
senses.definition: a tube or duct in the body that carries blood or another fluid
senses.definitionCN: 体内输送血液或其他液体的管道
senses.example: Cold makes the blood vessels in the fingers narrow.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷会让手指的血管收缩。
senses.why: The body borrows the container image: the tube holds and moves fluid the way a jug does.
senses.whyCN: 身体借用了容器意象：管道盛住并输送液体，正像一只水罐。

senses.title: A person as a bearer
senses.titleCN: （引申）承载者：作为载体的那个人
senses.definition: a person regarded as a bearer of a quality, a message or a role
senses.definitionCN: 被看作承载某种品质、信息或角色的人
senses.example: In the old story the youngest son is the vessel of the family's hope.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个老故事里，最小的儿子承载着全家的希望。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from thing to person: whoever holds and carries something onward is a vessel for it.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从物移到人：任何盛住并把某物传递下去的人，都是它的容器。

senses.title: A boat in a fixed sense
senses.definition: used in fixed names for types of boat, such as a patrol vessel or a research vessel
senses.definitionCN: 用于巡逻艇、科考船等固定船名说法中
senses.example: A research vessel spent three months mapping the sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一艘科考船花了三个月测绘海底。
senses.why: Here the container idea is frozen into a name for a job at sea.
senses.whyCN: 此时容器观念已经固化成一个命名海上职务的说法。

intro.en: Vessel came from Latin through Old French, and every sense still carries the idea of something hollow that holds.
intro.cn: vessel 经古法语来自拉丁语，每个义项都还带着「中空能盛」的观念。

items.en: Vas meant 'vessel, container, dish'; the plural vasa is still used in anatomy.
items.cn: vas 意为「容器、器皿、盘碟」，其复数 vasa 至今仍在解剖学中使用。

items.en: The diminutive vascellum meant 'a small vessel', and it is the form that reached French.
items.cn: 指小形式 vascellum 意为「小容器」，正是传到法语的那一形式。

items.en: Old French vaisseau meant both a container and a ship, keeping the two ideas together.
items.cn: 古法语 vaisseau 同时指容器与船，把两个观念放在一处。

items.en: English borrowed vessel in the thirteenth century, with ship, container and body-tube senses all present.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 vessel，船、容器与体内管道三个义项当时都已具备。

items.en: Nautical and medical usage split the word: a fishing vessel and a blood vessel barely meet.
items.cn: 航海与医学用法把这个词分开：渔船与血管几乎互不相干。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same container family; the near-meaning group gathers ships and containers with different shades.
note.cn: 形近组收同一容器词族的词；近义组收船只与容器类词，彼此侧重不同。

entries.definition: A decorative container for flowers; the Latin vas survives here too.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「花瓶」，同样来自拉丁语 vas。

entries.definition: The Latin word for vessel, used in anatomical terms such as vas deferens.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语原词，意为容器，用于 vas deferens 等解剖学术语。

entries.definition: A person who owes loyalty to a lord; an unrelated medieval word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「封臣」，来自中古拉丁语，与本词只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A large seagoing vessel; the general word beside the more formal vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「船」，是最通用的说法，vessel 更正式。

entries.definition: A smaller craft; vessel usually implies something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小船」，vessel 通常指更大的船。

entries.definition: Anything that holds something; broader and plainer than vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容器」，比 vessel 更宽泛、更朴素。

entries.definition: A tube in the body or a building; the clinical partner of vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「导管」，是 vessel 在医学语境中的伙伴词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vas and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vas，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: One word, three holders: a vessel carries people, water or blood.
normal.cn: 一个词，三种盛器：vessel 载人、盛水、运血。

normal.en: Latin vas is a container; a ship is a container you sail in.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vas 是容器；船就是你在里面航行的容器。

normal.en: Blood vessel and fishing vessel share the same shape of idea.
normal.cn: 血管与渔船共用同一个形状的观念。

normal.en: Vessel is more formal than ship; officials say vessel.
normal.cn: vessel 比 ship 更正式，官方文件多用 vessel。

normal.en: A vessel must be hollow: the inside matters more than the outside.
normal.cn: 器皿必须是中空的：里面比外面更重要。

abstract.en: Picture a clay jug on a table: the empty space is the useful part, and the clay only holds it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的一只陶罐：真正有用的是中间的空处，陶土只是把它围住。

abstract.en: The word then fills that emptiness with different contents: grain, oil, people, blood.
abstract.cn: 这个词随后用不同的内容填满那片空：谷物、油、人、血。

abstract.en: Anything that carries something safely across a distance can be called a vessel.
abstract.cn: 任何能把某物安全运送过一段距离的东西，都可以称为 vessel。

examples.en: A rescue vessel reached the sinking boat within twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 一艘救援船在二十分钟内赶到了那艘下沉的船旁。

examples.en: Store the oil in a sealed vessel away from heat.
examples.cn: 把油存放在远离热源的密封容器里。

examples.en: The doctor said the vessels around his heart were narrow.
examples.cn: 医生说他心脏周围的血管变窄了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维（ve）塞尔（ssel）」——维塞尔港口的船，一只会装货的大器皿：船；容器

root: 源自拉丁语 vas「容器」的指小形式 vascellum，经古法语 vaisseau「容器、船」进入英语；同源词有 vase、vas。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of vessel all share one hollow shape: a ship carrying people, a jug carrying liquid, a tube carrying blood, and by metaphor a person who carries a hope.
sensesIntro.cn: vessel 的五个义项共用同一个中空形状：船载人、罐盛液、管道运送血液，再经比喻指承载希望的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clay jug on a table, its hollow centre holding what is poured in.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的一只陶罐，中空处盛住倒进去的东西。

branches.en: CONTAINER LINE: the oldest layer, the jug on the table.
branches.cn: 容器线：最古老的一层，桌上的罐子。

branches.en: WATER LINE: the container grows large enough to sail in.
branches.cn: 水面线：容器大到可以航行其中，就成了船。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the same tube shape inside the body.
branches.cn: 体内线：身体内部同样的管状形态。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: a person becomes the vessel of a quality.
branches.cn: 比喻线：人成了某种品质的载体。

branches.en: CONTRAST: ship is plainer, vessel more formal and broader.
branches.cn: 对照线：ship 更朴素，vessel 更正式且范围更广。

intro.en: Vessel is a Latin diminutive that passed through French; the -el ending is a small reminder of its 'little container' origin.
intro.cn: vessel 是经法语而来的拉丁语指小形式；结尾 -el 隐约提示它「小容器」的出身。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vas, with the diminutive vascellum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vas 及其指小形式 vascellum。

definition_zh: 失事的船；残骸；事故；毁坏；使（船）失事
definition_en: a ship or vehicle destroyed in an accident, the broken remains of it, or to destroy something completely
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上，一艘龙骨断裂的船半埋进沙里
scene: 风暴过后的清晨，海边的浅滩上躺着一艘只剩骨架的船。 Divers found a wreck from the last century near the harbour mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 wreck 是「失事的船；残骸」（第 1 个义项：在事故中被毁的船或车，以及它剩下的残骸）；句意为潜水员在港口入口附近发现一艘上个世纪失事的船。退潮沙滩上那艘断了龙骨的船，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wreck 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「残骸；碎片」
由 wreck 加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「打捞船的人；拆毁者」
由 wreck 加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「失事的；被毁的」

senses.title: The broken ship
senses.definition: a ship, car, or plane that has been badly damaged or destroyed in an accident, or what is left of it
senses.definitionCN: 在事故中严重损坏或被毁的船、车或飞机，也指其残骸
senses.example: Divers found a wreck from the last century near the harbour mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在港口入口附近发现一艘上个世纪失事的船。
senses.why: Wreck first named a ship driven onto rocks and broken, so the object that survives an accident came to be called by its story.
senses.whyCN: wreck 最初指被风浪推上礁石撞碎的船，于是「经历事故后剩下的东西」就用这个故事的名称来称呼。

senses.title: The crash itself
senses.definition: an accident in which a vehicle is badly damaged or someone is badly hurt
senses.definitionCN: 车辆严重损坏或有人受重伤的事故
senses.example: The road was closed for hours after a wreck involving three trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 三辆卡车相撞的事故后，那条路封闭了几个小时。
senses.why: Because a broken hull is the visible result of a crash, the word moved from the result to the event that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 因为破碎的船体是撞毁事件看得见的结果，这个词就从结果移到了造成结果的事件上。

senses.title: A person in pieces
senses.definition: someone whose health, nerves, or life has been ruined, often in the phrase a nervous wreck
senses.definitionCN: 健康、精神或生活被摧毁的人，常见于说法 a nervous wreck
senses.example: After two sleepless nights she was a nervous wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 两个不眠之夜后，她的精神彻底垮了。
senses.why: If a body can be broken like a ship on rocks, then the same image describes a person whose nerves have cracked.
senses.whyCN: 如果身体可以像触礁的船一样被撞碎，那么同一个意象就能形容精神开裂的人。

senses.title: To break something apart
senses.definition: to damage or destroy something completely, or to cause a ship to break up
senses.definitionCN: 彻底损坏或摧毁某物，或使船破裂失事
senses.example: The storm wrecked two fishing boats on the same night.
senses.exampleCN: 那一夜风暴让两条渔船失事。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to give something the fate of the broken ship is to wreck it.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了动词：让某物遭遇破船的命运，就是 wreck it。

senses.title: The ruined plan
senses.definition: to spoil or ruin something such as a plan, a chance, or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、机会或关系等破灭或遭到破坏
senses.example: Heavy rain wrecked our plans for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨毁了我们的野餐计划。
senses.why: Abstract things are treated like fragile vessels, so whatever breaks them is said to wreck them.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的东西被当作易碎的容器，于是毁掉它们就说成 wreck。

intro.en: Wreck came into English from Old Norse and is related to the idea of something driven ashore and broken; the modern noun and verb grew from that picture.
intro.cn: wreck 由古诺斯语进入英语，本义与被冲上岸、撞碎的东西有关；现代的名词与动词都是从这幅画面长出来的。

items.en: The verb rekja and the noun wreck meant to drive something, especially a ship, ashore.
items.cn: 动词 rekja 与名词 wreck 意为把东西（尤指船）冲到岸上。

items.en: wrak or wrek named goods and ships cast up on the shore after a storm.
items.cn: wrak 或 wrek 指风暴后冲上岸的货物与船只。

items.en: Coastal law spoke of wreckum, the right to claim what the sea threw up.
items.cn: 沿海法律里说 wreckum，指认领大海抛上岸之物的权利。

items.en: The meaning widened from stranded ships to any vehicle or person that has been ruined.
items.cn: 词义从搁浅的船扩大到任何被毁的车辆或人。

items.en: The verb to wreck, meaning to ruin, is a later back-formation from the noun.
items.cn: 表示毁坏的动词 wreck 是由名词后期反向构成的。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same seamanship family, the second holds other words for ruin and disaster.
note.cn: 第一组收同一航海词族里的词，第二组收其他表示毁灭与灾难的词。

entries.definition: The broken parts left after a wreck.
A person or vehicle that clears away wrecks.
Destroyed or badly damaged.
To spoil or destroy something completely.
Scattered pieces left after something is destroyed.
The body of an old or broken ship.

normalIntro.en: Wreck is one syllable and starts with wr, the old English spelling habit that keeps the r silent.
normalIntro.cn: wreck 只有一个音节，以 wr 开头，这是英语里 r 不发音的老拼写习惯。

normal.en: The wr at the start is silent in the r, as in write and wrong.
normal.cn: 开头的 wr 里 r 不发音，write 与 wrong 也是这样。

normal.en: The same word gives shipwreck and wreckage.
normal.cn: 同一个词构成 shipwreck 与 wreckage。

normal.en: A nervous wreck borrows the image of a ship broken on rocks.
normal.cn: nervous wreck 借的是触礁碎船的意象。

normal.en: Wreck as a verb means to ruin, as in wreck the plan.
normal.cn: wreck 作动词意为毁掉，如 wreck the plan。

normal.en: Wreck is related to the Old Norse verb rekja, to drive ashore.
normal.cn: wreck 与古诺斯语动词 rekja（冲上岸）有关。

abstract.en: A broken keel sticking out of wet sand at low tide.
abstract.cn: 退潮时从湿沙里露出的断裂龙骨。

abstract.en: The silence after the wave has finished throwing things around.
abstract.cn: 浪把东西抛完之后的那片安静。

abstract.en: Something that once moved now lying still in pieces.
abstract.cn: 曾经会动的东西如今碎着躺下不动。

examples.en: The wreck of an old fishing boat was still visible at low tide.
examples.cn: 退潮时仍能看见一艘旧渔船的残骸。

examples.en: Two drivers were hurt in the wreck on the motorway.
examples.cn: 高速公路上的车祸中有两名司机受伤。

examples.en: The storm wrecked the harbour wall and flooded the village.
examples.cn: 风暴毁坏了码头墙，淹了村子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克」——礁石来克船，船就被克得只剩骨架。

root: 源自中古英语 wrak、wrek，来自古诺斯语 *wrek，本义为「被冲上岸的东西、漂来的残骸」，与 rekja（冲、赶）同源；同族词有 wreckage、wrecked。

sensesIntro.en: The broken ship comes first, then the crash that broke it, then the ruined person, then the act of ruining anything, then ruined plans.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有破碎的船，再有撞碎它的事故，然后是垮掉的人，接着是毁掉任何东西的动作，最后是破灭的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken hull half buried in sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：半埋在沙里的破碎船体。

branches.en: The object branch: what is left of the ship.
branches.cn: 实物分支：船剩下的东西。

branches.en: The event branch: the crash that produced the wreck.
branches.cn: 事件分支：造成残骸的那场撞毁。

branches.en: The human branch: a body broken like a ship.
branches.cn: 人分支：像船一样被撞碎的身体。

branches.en: The action branch: giving something the fate of a ship on rocks.
branches.cn: 动作分支：让某物经历触礁的船那样的命运。

branches.en: The image branch: both a ship and a person can end up in pieces.
branches.cn: 意象分支：船和人最后都可能碎成一堆。

intro.en: Wreck is a free stem borrowed from Old Norse; English added -age, -er and -ed to build the family around it.
intro.cn: wreck 是从古诺斯语借入的自由词干，英语在它周围加上 -age、-er、-ed 建成词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Norse, not Latin, so no Latin ancestor exists; the entries below are distant Indo-European cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自诺斯语而非拉丁语，因此没有拉丁语祖先；下面几条只是印欧语系的远亲。

items.meaning: the broken ship and the act of breaking
items.meaningCN: 破碎的船与毁坏的动作
items.example: The stem carries both the object and the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干同时承载物与动作。

items.example: Ship names the vessel and wreck names its fate.
items.exampleCN: ship 指明船只，wreck 指明它的命运。

items.meaning: a mass or collection of things
items.example: It forms wreckage, the mass of broken parts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wreckage，指成堆的残骸。

items.example: It forms wrecker, one who clears wrecks.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrecker，清理残骸的人。

items.example: It forms wrecked, having been destroyed.
The wrecked car blocked the lane.
items.exampleCN: 被撞毁的车堵住了车道。

items.meaning: the act of destroying or the moment of a crash
items.meaningCN: 毁坏的动作或撞毁的时刻
items.example: They cleared the wrecking site at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时清理了撞毁现场。

items.example: It is a different second element, but the sound recalls wreck.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分是不同的词，但读音让人想起 wreck。
